articles.body:
This is the beginning of your journey through the Holy Innocents' Cemetery, during your playthrough of Castlevania: Belmont's Curse . This is a continuation of our walkthrough, after successfully defeating The Warrior and descending the Prison Tower in Paris Streets . The Prophetess will be the third boss you fight in the game, although you may have already completed this fight if you decided to focus on them rather than going after The Warrior.

We begin at the Cemetery Entrance for the Holy Innocents' Cemetery region, an area separate from the Paris Streets that you've been exploring. You can head to the left, opening up this area, where a brief dialogue between Rose and The Fallen takes place, discussing the curse marked on her arm. A curse that was given to her Mother by Dracula and was passed down to her when she was born.

After this exchange, continue to make your way to the left. Expect to find undead rising from the ground, and glowing skulls appearing in the sky. However, many of these enemies should be familiar to you, and you can make short work of them.

Before you get too far, there's a platform with a purple anchor underneath it, allowing you to return to this section on your way back. Beneath it is a hidden wall that you can hit, exposing an XP statue.

With the statue destroyed, continue your way to the left until you reach a blocked wall with a bottom section that you cannot yet destroy, but will have to return with a specific upgrade to break it in the future. For now, use a wall-leap jump to reach the top, where you'll find a new encounter type for you to battle against.

At the center of the bottom section is a glowing casket, with multiple glowing undead enemies. Two of them are on platforms on opposite sides of the arena, with several undead enemies attached to the casket through the glowing green threads. You can destroy the Holy Cross throwing enemies as much as you like, but they'll continue to respawn. The ones in the center, however, are directly connected to the casket. Destroy them, and then you can damage the casket.

The enemies only stop spawning here after you've eliminated the casket. You can only do that if the enemies connected to it by the glowing green threads are destroyed first. Expect to see additional encounters similar to this as you continue making your way through the Cemetery.

With the casket eliminated and the glowing undead cleared, use your whip on the yellow anchor hovering above you. You'll need to swing to the right and get enough air to slash at the lever overlooking the upper left area, opening the door.

In the next location, you'll encounter a new enemy: a headless skeleton. The headless skeleton lashes forward, flailing as it does. You'll take damage when it hits you. What the skeleton is doing is going towards where its head is on the ground. When it reaches its head, it grabs it, looking to aim the head at you again to throw it. You'll take damage from the head if it hits you, and then have to dodge the flailing skeleton again. Your best bet is to get behind the skeleton, or use a Whip Attack, and deal with it that way. Expect to find more of them moving forward.

Continue your way to the left, and you'll unlock the Mirror of Life for the Cloister, a new section of the Cemetery.

From the Mirror of Life to the Cloister proper, as you enter the area, an undead walks toward you but is immediately destroyed by the chandelier above it.

All of the chandeliers in this area will fall on you, or an enemy, that gets too close under it. Expect it to begin to fall when you reach its halfway point, forcing you to continue moving forward, or quickly dive backward after you trigger it. You may be able to lure enemies underneath it to make short work of them, but expect them to be more troublesome for you than your foes.

After this initial start, make your way all the way to the left side of the room. However, as you attempt to reach the end, the final section gives out, sending you down below, taking you to a section known as the Sepulcher of the Knight.

Here, you'll encounter a Spirit, who provides you with additional details about The Prophetess. The Captain of the Guard had attempted to lead the others to the Roman Baths to deal with the creature, but was thwarted.

With this clue added, continue to head down, and you'll encounter a new type of enemy: floating Medusa heads (a good hint as to who The Prophetess is, and what you'll be facing later). You can hit and destroy these Medusa heads, but if you get too close, they face you and unleash a scream, causing you to become stone and locking you in place for a few seconds. They endlessly spawn and roll through their location, meaning it's better for you to bypass and avoid them than continually fight them.

When you get to the bottom, you'll find a golem that you can make short work of, and a glowing hallway to the left. There's a downward passage way to your right, but it is covered by an unbreakable surface, meaning you'll need to return to destroy it later.

Through the glowing door is a continuation of the Sepulcher of the Knight area, and you'll find yourself forced to slide underneath a small wall to head to the other side. You need to be quick, though, as the next area has breakable platforms for you to land on.

You'll need to jump across those broken platforms until you reach a yellow anchor, using your whip to swing up into the wall of spikes, reaching for the purple anchor at the center.

From that purple anchor, there is a second one, and then you can pivot to the right to reach another yellow anchor.

The swing from that yellow anchor should be enough for you to reach the upper right side, where you'll find another purple anchor to safely reach a sturdy platform.

Underneath that platform is a lower section with an XP statue, a purple anchor, and a lever. Break the statue and hit the lever, opening up the wall beneath you, allowing you to skip that entire jumping section if you come through here again.

You can now head to the upper right side and use the purple anchor to reach the glowing section door above you. This door brings you to a new section called the Memorial for the Dead.

From the entrance of the Memorial for the Dead, slide through the wall and use a wall-leap to reach the main area above you. In this area, there are a handful of undead enemies and a golem you have to dispatch.

With those foes eliminated, rather than continuing to the left, explore the rest of this room by jumping up the platforms to the upper areas. You'll find a few more undead enemies and glowing skulls that continue to spawn, no matter how many times you eliminate them.

Make sure to destroy the XP statue on the far left side of the room before making your way to the right. Here, you'll find a glowing door and a gargoyle above you.

Although it is stationary, it's a new type of enemy. You can use your whip to reach up and grab the purple anchor above it, and go through the grate to destroy the XP statue. However, after hitting the gargoyle and going out of range from it, expect it to come alive and start moving around and attacking you. It will attempt to swipe at you and spit fireballs when you're too far away from it. Dispatch it before heading into the next section.

This door takes you back to the Cloister, and you're on the other side of where you originally fell through into the Sepulcher of the Knight. Hit the lever, and you'll cause a door to go over the top of that section, ensuring you go back down there. You can now use the purple anchor above you to go through the door and explore the upper section of the Cloister. This route will unlock another section of the map, and unlock a new relic.

In this upper section, you'll encounter several familiar enemies, like the undead with the Holy Cross, the gargoyle, and the never-dying flaming skulls.

Take these enemies out at the entrance, and jump onto the platform where the undead tossing crosses was, jumping over and using your whip on the yellow anchor.

Swing on the yellow anchor going up to a higher area where you'll face off against a headless undead charging at you. Dispatch them, and then drop down, dealing with the golem beneath you.

From the golem, continue making your way to the right side, avoiding the spikes beneath you. There's anotehr golem further down the right path that you have to eliminate. Once they're dealt with, before going through the glowing door, jump over the spike pit you just came from, and attempt to swing onto the yellow anchor.

You want to swing on top of that upper section and hold onto the wall, jumping over to the left side, revealing a hidden wall. An undead swordsman will be here that you can quickly dispatch before sliding underneath the wall, revealing a Wise Heart that you can collect.

With the Wise Heart in your collection, head back to the rightmost glowing down, and head through.

This brings you to the Cemetery Entrance once again, overlooking a section you crossed before heading into the Cloister. Drop down and hit the lever connecting the two areas. There's also a small section of wall protected by abyss shards. You can bypass them by using your Halo of Light, and from there, swing onto the yellow anchors to the right of you.

Swing across this upper section, and you'll reach a higher platform with a chest.

Open the chest to reveal the Abyssal Eye relic ( Rose deals 35% more damage to controlled enemies ), and you can choose to begin using it as one of your three relics, or keep it in your collection.

Once you've collected the Abyssal Eye, make your way back to the Memorial for the Dead section of the map. Here's the location for reference, and you'll find a glowing door at this location that takes you to another part of the map, taking you to the Fountain of the Innocents.

Before you get too far into this entrance, there's a gargoyle at the beginning. Treat it like an anchor, and throw your whip up to reach this higher section.

You want to jump onto the breakable planks and jump to the right, using your whip on the yellow anchor. Swing to the left, turn around, reattach to it, and swing to the right, reaching the upper platform above the Fountain of the Innocents entrance, where you'll find a glowing down.

Head through the glowing down, and you'll drop down a section with spike walls on either side, and there will be an XP statue at the bottom. Fall through the grate below it to return to the Fountain entrance. However, before you leave, there's another relic you can grab and add to your collection.

Now, slide under the wall to your left, and you'll land on a breakable platform. You need to be quick, as you have to slide to the right immediately when you land, revealing an invisible wall and a lever. If you miss, you can try again, as the breakable wall will come back together after a few seconds. Hitting this lever removes the wall that was on the glowing door leading below, to your left.

Make your way down, and you'll enter the Pillaged Tombs and immediately start an encounter.

At the center of this encounter is a glowing green casket. On the upper platforms will be a pair of undead throwing Holy Crosses that you can eliminate, but they shouldn't be your main focus.

You want to wait for the pair of golems to appear, as they'll have green threads attached to them. When they show up, go for and eliminate them as quickly as possible. When they're gone, the casket will be unprotected, allowing you to destroy it and end the encounter.

With those eliminated, proceed to the right, and you'll find the relic chest with the Nightshade relic inside it ( using a healing potion recovers 40% of maximum mana ).

When you're ready to leave, head back to the central room and use the yellow anchors to swing onto the platforms, then swing up to the glowing door to return to the Fountain entrance. From there, you want to follow the route that you took to find that hidden XP statue in the Memorial for the Dead room.

However, when you're on the breakable platforms, swing all the way to the left, and you'll see a purple anchor on the other side.

You'll land on the upper section of where you were to grab the Nightshade. Slide underneath the wall and fall down to break the debris to open the door, connecting these two locations, ensuring you don't have to take the upper anchors again to reach this spot.

Now, slide under the wall to the next area, and you'll be on your path to the fountain.

Ahead, you'll encounter a gargoyle on the other side, along with undead foes and a golem below a platform. Dispatch these foes, and there's a small, hidden wall beneath the platform. If you slide through it, there's a wall chicken that you can pick up to heal yourself.

From this path, continue going to the left, and you'll find yourself beneath a second floor that you won't be able to reach, regardless of how you attempt to wall-leap. You need to head to the left room, where you'll find a lever in the center.

Hit the lever, causing the wall to drop down in the open section that you were probably struggling to get through to reach the second floor, along with a handful of enemies.

Defeat the foes, and then return to where you were performing that wall jump to reach that XP statue.

You should have an easier time reaching this upper section and the XP statue.

Continue to the left, and you'll find a golden chest, revealing a new weapon to add to your arsenal: the lance.

You'll have an opportunity to test this weapon as multiple enemies spawn around you. Your path is also blocked until you defeat these foes, giving you the chance to test your skills and try your hand at throwing the spear during combat, especially as you fight a new enemy, a large crow. The crow stays close to the corners of the screen, forcing you to use the ranged attack of the lance, or you can jump into the air to use your whip attack to get close to it. It has a hefty ranged attack that fires a wave of smaller crows at you, forcing you to dodge out of the way to avoid them.

Once you've completed this part and unlocked this weapon, head back to the Fountain of the Lost. You may have noticed that when you were crossing the gap of water, there's a bubbling visual at the surface.

You want to dive into this section of the water, and you'll discover a hidden path available for you to explore. This brings you to a lower section known as the Serpent's Lair.

When you drop down into the Serpent's Lair from this section, you'll notice a large chest with four chains connected to it, and it is not a part of the larger story at this point. For the primary objectives, we won't be trying to unravel this mystery at the moment, but we'll be back to it at a later point.

Right now, continue to descend and head down one left. On the right side, you'll find an XP statue, opposite a glowing door.

While the glowing door is a section to explore, I recommend heading to the bottom of this chamber. As you do, when you reach the bottom, there's a Mirror of Life for you to unlock on the right side. Head through the right door, and you'll unlock the Ancient Sewers Mirror of Life.

After unlocking this location, return to the Serpents' Lair and head down to the left, where you'll find a boss door. This will bring you back to facing off against the next guardian: The Prophetess.

Upon entering the boss room, you'll begin a quick cutscene with The Fallen pointing out the beauty of the ruins. It's short-lived as Rose points out the sound of snakes, and she finds herself face-to-face with Medusa, the next guardian. Medusa was an adversary that Trevor and Sypha had previously fought and killed, but it appears they were mistaken, and Rose has to finish what her family started.

Before starting this fight, I recommend equipping the Lance and the Holy Cross Arcana to your character. These are some of the best weapons to use against Medusa, as the extended range of the lance can provide more opportunities to damage this boss compared to the other weapons.

While these are the best weapon and magic combinations I recommend, the choice is entirely up to your playstyle and what you prefer!

When the boss fight begins, you'll be standing next to Medusa, who will take a swipe at you. Her melee attacks are slow and easy to telegraph, but they can be punishing if she does manage to hit you. After the first strike, she bundles her snake hair together and attempts to swipe twice in front of her. This is the first attack combination you need to watch out for throughout this encounter.

The second is her petrifying ray. She charges this up and sends out a blast of green-white energy in front of her. If you're facing her, she freezes you for a moment (similar to when the smaller Medusa heads petrify you), and you'll need to break out of it. However, if you're hit by it and not facing her, the attack does nothing.

The melee combo is what she'll use against you when you're standing on a platform in front of her. If you're standing away from her, she'll hit you with the petrifying ray. When you stay too long at a distance from her, she'll descend into the water and switch sides. She'll lash out with her tail at the lower section of the boss arena when this happens as well. However, her tail can still lash out on the bottom even if she's above the water, so always watch out for it if you decide to head to a lower section while she's up top.

When you get her down to close to 70% of her health, Medusa enters a frenzy. She lashes out with her claws and madly attacks in front of her, while her tail lashes out below, flailing from side to side on the lower platforms. While this is going on, I recommend heading to the opposite side of the arena and waiting for this to subside, using any ranged attacks you might have to hit her while you have the opportunity.

As this frenzy is happening, Medusa's tail will knock loose a rock and send it to the bottom side, opposite of her. You want to race over there as quickly as possible, as Medusa is about to unleash an arena-wide petrifying ray that can heavily damage you if you are not behind this rock. She telegraphs this with a large, single ray that follows you for a few seconds before she unleashes the arena-wide blast. Again, you can't block or dodge it, beyond hiding behind this rock. You have to wait until she's finished firing her rays, and then the rock is destroyed, before returning to your fight against her.

You can expect the same attack pattern from Medusa after the first ray blast from her. However, a change is that the smaller Medusa heads will begin spawning throughout the arena, and you'll need to avoid or defeat those alongside fighting Medusa. Taking these out might be better, as it prevents them from getting too close and petrifying you halfway through an attack combo or a dodge.

The overall pattern remains the same throughout the fight. You can expect the arena-wide blast from Medusa when you get her to 70%, 50%, and 25% health, so she'll only do it three times against you. During the portions when you get her to 50% and 25%, smaller rocks do fall that can damage you. Additionally, when her tail lashes below, these smaller rocks can fall, and you'll need to be on the lookout for those. Beyond those small changes, Medusa's attacks and attack pattern remain the same until you defeat her.

When she falls, you'll be able to add Medusa's Arcana to your Tarot cards, unlocking the Petrifying Gaze spell and receiving the fallen Guardian key that you can use to unlock the Catacombs.

With Medusa defeated, the two Guardians have been put down, and you can bring the last key to the Catacombs door. You can reach this location by returning to where you originally fought The Fallen under the Paris Streets, in the sewers.

To reach that point, return to the Ancient Sewers Mirror of Life, as this offers the best route out of the Serpents' Lair. As you leave Medusa's boss room, the statue that was holding the sword and shield will disappear, and you can pick up those weapons, unlocking the Rusted Harpè and Aegis weapons. Unlike other weapons, you won't be blocked and forced to test them out against waves of enemies, thankfully.

After healing at the Ancient Sewers Mirror of Life, proceed to the glowing door on the right and head through the Ancient Sewers. At the entrance, you'll need to use your whip attack on the Medusa heads that are spawning above you to reach the upper platform.

For this next section, you'll need to be quick. There are plenty of breakable platforms and purple anchors that you need to aim at to proceed to the next section.

At the start, stand on the breakable platform and jump up to whip-attack the first purple anchor. Jump over the initial pit of spikes, hitting the second purple anchor on the right.

You'll be able to rest on the wall for a few seconds before dropping down to another breakable platform and sliding to the right, which connects to a third breakable platform. Above you is another purple anchor you can grab, and from there, jump up to the next breakable platform. You'll need to watch out for the moving Medusa heads, as they may interrupt you if you're not fast enough.

Once you've cleared those, you can jump to the upper platform where the Medusa heads are stopping and slide under the wall, completing this section.

You can jump down through a grate here and encounter multiple fish enemies and the large crow. After they've been dispatched, head below to the next section where you'll find another pair of fish enemies and an undead swordsman.

With all of those enemies cleared, head to the bottom area of the Ancient Sewers. Similar to the entrance of this area, you'll need to be quick. You want to drop down onto the breakable platform and activate the Halo of Light to bypass the abyss shards on the right.

You can quickly jump to the right in this area and continue down, where you'll find a door to take you back to the Paris Streets region.

This brings you to the bottom of the Central Sewer Drain in the Paris Streets region, allowing you to break down the barrier holding a door back and connecting to these areas.

You can now make your way to the right and return to the Gate to the Catacombs next to the Path of the Rat.

When you arrive, interact with the catacomb gateway, and you'll begin a cutscene with Rose placing the remaining gems at the door. Joan and The Fallen warn Rose about heading down, suggesting that it might be a good idea to get her father. Rose insists that she face this threat alone, with Medusa encouraging her to face her destiny.

After the quick discussion, you can head below and enter the new area, unlocking the Catacombs of Paris and a new region and threat for you to face.

articles.title: Catacombs of Paris Walkthrough - Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Catacombs of Paris become available after defeating The Fallen, The Warrior, and The Prophetess in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. These bosses hold the
articles.body:
The Catacombs of Paris become available after defeating The Fallen , The Warrior , and The Prophetess in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse . These bosses hold the gems that unlock passage to this section of the game, which leads Rose down, deep underneath the city of Paris, as she faces off against the one who is channeling a powerful ritual to bring back Lord Dracula.

You'll begin your journey with Rose at the Catacombs Entrance, shortly after you've opened up the Gateway.

From this section of the map, your only choice is to descend from the entrance and then take the passageway to your left through the glowing door.

Taking this path, expect to find multiple flaming skulls through this hallway. However, you can ignore them and focus on reaching the leftmost wall, where you'll reach a blocked path with a floor made up of abyss shards.

You can use your Halo of Light to get through them, heading to the lower section where you'll encounter a new enemy, a small spider-skull-like creature crawling on the floor.

The creature does not move much, but spits out fireballs at you. If you hit it, the creature begins glowing, and the glow begins to flash as it rushes around the floor, attempting to get closer to you. After a few seconds, the creature explodes, unleashing a small area of damage if you're nearby. You'll want to stay away from the creature while this happens, and avoid it until it explodes. Expect to find more throughout the Catacombs.

Before you get too far away from this section, jump on the wall above the grate that takes you down to find an XP statue hidden above you.

After breaking down, head down, and you'll land on a pile of abyss shards. You'll need to use your Halo of Light to get through, and in the next room are an undead archer and a red, unkillable skeleton. Make your way past them through the abyss shards on the left side, and slide down to the lowest floor. There, you'll meet another new foe.

It's a stack of dragon skulls, one facing away and the other toward you. These skulls have two attacks: a ranged fireball that they spit out, and a flamethrower that they use when you get close. These skulls can pivot in your direction, so don't expect them to face away from you for too long. Thankfully, they are stationary, and you can make short work of them using your Holy Cross or any of your melee attacks.

Once they're defeated, follow the right path, and you'll find a green glowing symbol against the wall. Although you don't have much information about this symbol, it's important to note and look for it throughout your time exploring the Catacombs. Proceed through the glowing door when you're ready.

In the next room, you'll be faced with several routes that you can explore. The path you want to focus on is going upwards, using the abyssal shards as walls to leap up to the top. You want to reach the section with the abyssal shards above you, using the Halo of Light to bypass them. You can then rest at this part to use it like a checkpoint.

From there, jump onto the leftmost abyssal shard wall, and jump off that, using the Halo of Light to bypass the next wall and land on the other side. Stop at the abyssal shards above the spike pits, and then destroy the dragon skulls on your right.

After defeating them, a pair of ghouls will leap out at you when you reach the end of that hallway. When they're defeated, leap up and follow the path upward, taking the glowing door to the area above you.

Along this side path, you'll find multiple rolling blades on the outer sides of these walls. You'll need to carefully skirt them, mixing your whip leap with your Halo of Light. First, jump up to attach the purple anchor above you, and then grab the wall to your left.

You can safely land on the abyssal shards below the second anchor and take a break.

After you clear this section, give yourself a small jump forward, activating your Halo of Light. You'll be able to bypass the abyssal shards on the left and attach yourself to the yellow anchor, swinging to the far left. Follow the entire swing forward, keeping the Halo of Light activated, and you'll land above. Once you clear these shards, turn off the Halo, and you'll safely land here.

For this section, you repeat much of the same jump, leaping down and waiting until you can grab the second anchor of light, and swing to the left. When you reach the end of the swing, let go, and then perform it again to grab the purple anchor on the far left. Carefully drop directly below this anchor, and you'll reach the bottom.

You'll find the Brave Heart for the Catacomb Entrance at this location. You can now slide through the small wall to your right using your Halo to return to the starting point, and then head to the bottom right to continue going further into the Catacombs.

In the room to the right as you pass through the abyssal shards, there are multiple enemies you'll have to clear. Many are ones you've seen before, so they shouldn't be too much of a surprise. I recommend focusing on the golem first, followed by the ghouls, before working on the smaller foes. Proceed to the right glowing down when you eliminate them, taking you to the Path of the Abyss.

The start to the Path of the Abyss should be a quick one. There are a pair of undead archers and golems in this room. Make short work of them, and continue down to the far right side, through the glowing door.

Through here, you'll be blocked by an abyssal wall, with multiple rolling blades in front of you. The one on the bottom is consistently moving back and forth. Use your Halo of Light to bypass the shards when the rolling blade is close to you, and follow it through the other side. Wait in the middle until it starts to roll back to you, and then jump over it, going through the grate to the area below.

You'll find a stack of three dragon skulls waiting for you, and more rolling blades in the next room. For these blades, there's one moving along a large platform. Wait until it begins to go down before jumping across, making it to far left of the platform. You can jump down when you clear this, being careful for when the blade rotates back around to the top section you're walking on. It's important to note there's another blade on the bottom that's also moving, but it should give you plenty of room to move across.

When you reach the bottom, wait until the upper blade is on the left wall (same side as you), and the bottom blade is moving forward.

You can run along the hallway when the lower blade is on this side, before it comes back, and you can jump over it. You should then be able to perform another jump over a pit of spikes before jumping down to the next section.

As you might have expected, more blades! Thankfully, only the one this time. It's rolling across the top of the section you need to pass, with a pair of purple anchors. You can ignore the one on your side (as you'll need it if you ever come back this way). You need to wait until the blade is on the far left side before jumping into the pit. When you're halfway to the spikes, use your whip to reach the leftmost purple anchor, flinging Rose across.

You should miss the blade as it moves back to the right side, and safely make it to the left wall, allowing you to jump to the section below. No more blades this time, only a glowing door that takes you to the Quarry Elevator.

As you reach this section, there's a Mirror of Life on your path! Follow the path to the left to unlock it.

Head to the pathway on the left, and you'll reach the Crossroads of the Dead, but this section is not too much of a concern for you right now.

You want to continue going down the path to the left, taking you to the Charnel Galleries. There will be a wall of abyss shards in your way that you can go through using your Halo.

Another set of abyss shards will block your path ahead, and when you pass through them, make sure to turn it off as you successfully cut through them. There are shards on the ground you want to use to catch yourself, making sure you don't hit the spikes below. From there, head to the top and go through the glowing door next to the purple anchor.

In this next room, there will be an entire section of rolling blades moving counter-clockwise. You want to enter this room as the blades are moving to the right, so you're right behind them. From there, wait one second, and then jump onto the wall, wall-leaping behind a blade, as one will be below you, haunting you each step.

As the blade in front of you goes to the left, follow it onto the upper platform, and then race to the left side, making a jump to reach the purple anchor above you. This brings you to a ledge where you can take a break.

There is another blade above you, but it won't reach down to hit you, giving you plenty of room to rest here. When the blade is rolling up, wall-leap up to the next hallway, and stop at the glowing door.

Above you is a grate with a Spirit that you can speak with. Talk to the Spirit, and they'll provide further context to the green markings on the wall.

The spirit reveals that they belong to the one who had been dragging the souls down from Paris, taking them to the Altar of Bones. The marks on the wall lead to this section, and where you'll be facing your next adversary: the Shadow. You'll receive this Tarot card in this moment, and the markings on the wall will appear on your map, should you get lost down here.

After speaking with the Spirit, take the path to your left and fall down the area with spike walls. When you reach the bottom, you'll appear on the other side of the puzzle next to a level, connecting these two areas. You can take the purple anchors up if you want to return to the glowing door above you, rather than taking the path full of blades.

You can make your way back down to the start of this puzzle, where you jumped onto this path using the purple anchor. Rather than going back down to the Crossroads of the Dead, head to the left and follow the green markings on the wall.

In this next section, you'll enter a soon-to-be blocked-off room as multiple enemies spawn here. None of them should be new to you, as you have to eliminate them to continue your path to the right side.

However, the final enemy is a skeleton ogre, which hasn't appeared for quite some time. You'll want to make some room between it and you, utilizing the purple anchors to make short work of it. When it's down, continue on the pathway to the right side.

You'll enter a hallway, underneath where you were in the Crossroads of the Dead. Halfway along this path is a lever, and hitting it will cause the bone bridges to move down, allowing you to descend further. I, however, recommend taking the path back up for a short time to save at the Mirror of Life before going down.

You need to follow the path you made using the lever. Follow down the slope to the right side, taking down a few ghouls along the way, and enter the Chamber of Whispers.

This is a tricky area that requires quick use of your whip and Halo, as it involves more blades. Wait for the pair of blades to move to the right side before jumping onto the path, before following after them.

Here, you can choose whether you want to jump down the abyss shards or use your whip on the purple anchor. The purple anchor is faster, but jumping down is safer. If you jump down, wait for the shards to go to the left before jumping up and racing to the right side. If you choose the purple anchor, wait until they start to rotate back to you before using it.

From here, jump onto the platform of abyss shards. You can only be here for a few seconds, as the blades are likely already returning. Jump to the right through the abyss wall, use your whip to grab the anchor, and fall down.

You can jump down to the lower section to clear this area, where you'll find more blades. Wait until these blades are moving to the left before moving onto the path.

You'll be standing on abyss shards during this section. You want to wait until the blades are going toward you before you activate the Halo and fall down. When they're on the right side, jump up (keeping the Halo active), and return to the path, turning the Halo off after this section and race to the left side. You can use your whip to hit the leftmost purple anchor to help clear this section.

After this is finished, jump up to the green mark and hit the left, moving a section of the Crossroads of the Dead. You can now drop down and go through the glowing door, taking you back to this area.

As you return to the Crossroads of the Dead, this section might seem like you've hit a brick wall. As you go all the way to the left side, you'll enter a dead-end chamber with a red skeleton inside it (however, it does have an XP statue in here).

Instead, head to the center of the Crossroads of the Dead, where the purple anchor is. Use it to lift yourself up, and head through the wall.

When you're through the wall, go to the right side, and you'll end up behind the door to the left of the lever. You can break it, and then pass through the glowing door to be in the upper section, next to the golden chest.

You can open it up to unlock the Pair of Longswords, a new weapon available to you for those who prefer close-range, rapid dual-blade attacks.

Here, you can continue to the left and hit a lever to knock the bone arms down, allowing you to make your way further down into the Crossroads of the Dead. You'll encounter a few ghouls in the bottom section before going further to the left, through another glowing door. This will take you to the Gallery of Teeth.

Here, you'll enter a relatively simple section, or so it appears. You'll encounter a simple skeleton and be able to proceed further down the hallway to the left. However, when you get close to the end, a veil over the floor disappears, and you'll fall through. A pair of ghouls will be waiting for you, and you have to eliminate them.

Once they're dealt with, if you destroy the wall to your left, you'll see that you need to go back. Head to the far left, climb the wall, and then use the purple anchor above where you fell to return to your path. Where you were fighting that skeleton is a grate that you can fall down, where you can see another distinct green marking.

This path brings you to another glowing door, and back to the Crossroads of the Dead. Take the path to the right, and you'll find another lever, lowering the bridge so you can head down. Expect ghouls to jump at you as you have another glowing door to explore. This brings you to a lower section of the Gallery of Teeth, underneath where you were.

For this section, it's another opportunity to test your skills at timing your jumps, and using your whip. For this first part, step onto the shards and wait for the blade to be up or down. Jump across, and you'll land on another platform of shards.

You'll need to make another jump, but you have to activate your Halo to bypass it. You don't have long to rest, though, as this is a breakaway platform. When you land, jump across, but deactivate your Halo to rest on the shards.

From this platform, jump over the blade when it's above or below you, and use your whip to attach to the purple anchor on the other side. You also need to have your Halo on to go through the shards, and there's another breakaway platform. You'll have to jump one more time, on the left side, along the wall of spikes to land below.

Again, there's another breakaway platform waiting for you. Quickly go to the left (with your Halo still on), and you can take a rest on this platform before facing off against more blades.

In this section, it's all about quick movement. You'll need to keep your Halo active and jump to the right, landing on the shards platform between the pair of blades. Wait until the second blade is up or down, and then make the jump again.

On this second platform, wait for the blade to be up or down before using your whip to reach the purple anchor. Here, make sure the Halo is on, and you can bypass these shards. However, deactivate the Halo when you're through, and land on the shards to complete this area.

There's one last blade you need to avoid, but it's on a regular platform, and there's a glowing door on your far right.

You'll make your way to the Crossroads of the Dead, next to a lever. When you activate it, you'll go through the floor and face off against a ghoul.

After defeating it, hit the second, true lever, and then you can jump up the wall from the way you came, and hit the purple anchor on the far right to return to the proper Crossroads of the Dead area, above you.

Take the path to the right, with a few enemies waiting for you as you make your way to the glowing door on the right side. This brings you to the De Rais Necropolis.

In the next room, when you enter the central chamber, two different sets of dragon skulls drop on either side of you. There are also glowing skulls that you'll have to fight that appear above you. You should be able to quickly dispatch them, but watch out for the breakaway platforms in the room before moving ahead.

You can jump down a grate to a lower section where a pile of dragon skulls are blocking your path. You have to attack them from above (or jump down to any of the lower levels) to dispatch them. I recommend hitting them from above as they won't be able to aim or attack you, but the sides are much faster.

When you reach the bottom, slide underneath the wall and head into the chamber on the left. There will be an enemy encounter in here with multiple waves, featuring a variety of skeletons, ghouls, and golems spawning on the bottom and upper platforms. You can use the yellow anchors to reach hard-to-reach enemies on top.

After dispatching them, head to the left and enter the Jaws of Limbo. You can explore the chamber on the right, but this primary section is the main area you want to explore.

At the center of this chamber, use the yellow anchor to swing up and hit the lever on top, allowing you to descend to the lower section, bringing you to the Throat of Hell.

Before you get too far, dip over to the left side using the yellow anchor, and you'll find the Throat of Hell Wise Heart before making your way to the left.

Continue your way to the left, taking the yellow anchor, and then go through the glowing gate to head into the Condemned Mineshaft. Continue your path to the right, and stop at the halfway as you drop down from the grate, where you'll find an elevator. Take the elevator up, and it'll bring you to the Quarry Elevator. Hit the lever to the left of it, connecting these two locations. You can run over to the Quarry Elevator Mirror of Life before heading back down to the Condemned Mineshaft

When you're back in the Condemned Mineshaft, there's another elevator on your left, but it's blocked by a door. Head to the right instead, where you'll find a ghoul and a small pile of dragon bones. Dispatch them, and head through the glowing door.

This will bring you to the Blood Pits, and a room full of spikes with the spider skulls crawling around. Use your whip to hit the first one, and then land on the second platform, destroying the second one if you feel you must. Jump down from here, and there will be a third on a further wall, with a golem between you two. Dispatch them all, and head to the far right, where you'll be above a grate and another glowing green mark.

Follow the path below, and head into the far left, or the central chamber below you. Both are correct paths, and full of enemies. If you go through the central chamber, dispatch all of the foes here, and then head to the bottom right, where there's an exposed wall that you can break through, and go below.

If you go the leftmost path, head down, take out the enemies there, and continue downward. You'll go through a side chamber after landing from a breakaway platform (which won't let you back up when it rebuilds). Defeat the enemies here, but head to the left side where there's another breakaway chamber, and destroy the wall, revealing another XP statue. You can then take the grate on the right down and enter the main path, continuing your descent below.

Before you get too far, stop at the grate with a purple chamber and break the wall to the right of it. You'll reveal another XP statue that you should destroy before heading below.

In this lower section, there is a small section that you can slide under on the far left side. Go through it, and you'll see an abyss wall that you can bypass using your Halo.

On the other side is a breakaway platform, and you want to deactivate your Halo to climb up, making your way to the top. At the top, reactivate your Halo, and you'll be able to reach a hidden Brave Heart, adding it to your collection for the Blood Pits.

Return to the start of this quick puzzle, and head down through the grate. There's a large pit of water (blood) below that you can jump over using the yellow anchor, taking you to the other side and through a glowing door.

There's a brief golem encounter after this chamber, but you can make short work of it. As you continue to the left, there's a large spinning blade above you that goes back and forth. Thankfully, it's on the top, so it shouldn't take too much effort to dodge as you go from one side to the other.

When you can drop down on the far left side, there's a breakaway platform that you need to watch out for. Quickly move to the right, and you'll avoid the spikes. Here, things become a bit trickier.

The spinning blades in this section are much closer together. For me, I waited until the one on top was on the far right, and the lower one was much further to the right.

When the top one began to move back, I jumped on the wall, jumped over it, and waited on the wall for a few seconds. Hold here until the lower blade gets down to where you were previously, and then jump onto the upper platform, continuing to the right. You can jump down from here safely.

At this point, head to the right side, break the wall, and enter a new area called the Hall of the Fallen Angels. At the entrance, you'll find a golden chest, revealing the final weapon for you to unlock: the Whip.

The iconic weapon of the Belmont family. A quick dialogue will happen between Rose and all of the spirits from the Tarot Arcana, before a fight breaks out, allowing you to test out the weapon if you choose to do so.

When the fight is complete, fall through the grate at the center of the room and head down, bringing you to the Stairway to Hell.

You'll be taking a left path in the Stairway to Hell section, where a pair of ghouls drop down from the ceiling to attack you during this section. After dispatching them, head to the area below and face off against a skeleton ogre.

After dealing with the ogre, follow the right path and fall through the grate. Continue your pathing to the left side, and prepare to be ambushed by five ghouls dropping from the ceiling. It's a perfect time to potentially get all five kills with your Holy Cross, if you can do it!

There is a glowing door at the end of the hallway, taking you to the lower section of Stairway to Hell. Here, you'll make your way down and find a blocked door. Jump down through the grate, and head to the left, bringing yourself up using the purple anchor, and hit the lever on the left side. This should open up the right wall, along with the wall next to the boss door.

However, before going too much further, take the elevator above you. This will bring you back to the Condemned Mineshaft, and you can hit the lever here to connect it to the main room before heading back down and into the boss room.

Rose adds a comment as you cross the threshold of this door, eager to face off against the one bringing Dracula back to life. The Fallen warns her it could be dangerous, but Rose dismisses it, believing he was still attempting to serve the one bringing Dracula back to life before she enters the chamber.

A cutscene begins when Rose enters the room, as the many souls of France are poured into what is likely Dracula. Here, we see the Shadow, and it's revealed that they are Death, a being that Rose knows about from her father's time as a Vampire Hunter.

Although Death is surprised to see Rose here, it cares not. He's happy to have a Belmont in his vicinity, to help finish the ritual and bring Dracula back to life.

After the conversation, a battle begins against Death. However, none of your attacks work against this entity at this time. You won't be able to damage Death here, and it will make short work of you during this encounter.

When it's over, a much longer cutscene occurs, showing the success of Death's ritual to bring back Count Dracula. Not only has Dracula returned, but his castle rises over the ashes of Paris, and he resides inside it, eager to regain his full strength.

As the cutscene plays out, Trevor appears to save Rose, allowing her to escape but at the cost of his arm as he faces off against Death.

With Rose cut off from her father, she learns here that the Guardians she defeated were there to assist her (not Medusa). As it turns out, her ancestor, Leon, is the true identity of The Fallen. He had been captured and possessed by Count Dracula four centuries ago, but after being beat by Rose and through the power of the Tarot cards, his mind has become free.

He vows to help Rose and help her seek justice against Count Dracula. The first step to achieve this is to reach his castle.

From your starting point at the Collapsed Path of Orpheus, head to the left side of the chamber and use the purple anchor to hoist yourself up to the top section.

From here, take a left, and use your Halo to bypass the shards. However, you'll need to quickly deactivate it and use the forward shards to reach the upper area. There's a breakable platform underneath you, so you don't have time to stand here for long.

When you reach the top, head to the left and activate your Halo again to bypass the shard wall to your left. However, there's another breakable platform underneath you, so there's little time for you to react. You'll need to jump out of the shards, deactivate the Halo quickly, and wall-leap on the shards to reach the top.

When you get close to the top, activate your Halo again and use your whip to catch the yellow anchor on the upper right side. You can use it to swing up to the top, keeping the Halo active as there's another wall of shards in your way. When those shards are cleared, deactivate the Halo to remain on this upper section and grab onto the purple anchor, and make your way to the right. You'll have to slide through the wall to make it to the next room.

Here, you'll find a purple anchor above you. Jump to grab it, and then jump to the breakable platform. It won't last long, and you might have time to leap over the spike wall, but it's better to use the secondary purple anchor on the right side to safely land. You'll find a glowing door on the right side, bringing you to a larger room.

In this larger room, make your way to the far right side where you'll find a shard wall. Use your Halo to bypass it, but there's a breakable platform below you and to your right. When you're on this platform, lower the Halo, jump on the rightmost breakable platform, and use it to get on top of the shards.

At the top, there's a yellow anchor you can use to swing, but there's nowhere to go on the left side. Follow through on the swing for the left side, and then turn around to perform it on the right.

You'll find a second yellow anchor to your right, and you can take it to the upper section where you'll find a breakable platform.

Bounce off that breakable platform to discover a third yellow anchor higher above you. Swing off that and proceed to the left side, where you'll meet a wall of shards. Use your Halo to bypass them, and then deactivate the Halo once you're clear to safely land on them. Proceed to the glowing door on your left once you're finished.

For this room, you'll be switching between turning your Halo off and on at specific times, providing good practice for mastering it while also using your jump and whip leaps to get to the top. For this first part, activate your Halo and go through the yellow anchor, swinging to the left side.

After you've cleared that, deactivate the Halo and jump onto the shard wall on the left side. Use this jump to reach the upper platform on top of a bed of spikes. However, this is a breakable platform and shatters after a few seconds. You can't rest here.

You have to immediately activate your Halo once again and jump to the right, swinging on the yellow anchor. Again, you can't leave your Halo activated for too long after you clear these shards, as a wall of shards protects you from the rightmost spikes. After you clear the shards, let go of the yellow anchor and deactivate the Halo to bounce off the wall and land on the upper platform. It's breakable again, forcing you to continue your forward momentum to the left.

There's another yellow anchor on this side that you can use, jumping to the second platform and using it to swing up to the left. It's a narrow passage, but above you are a pair of purple anchors. You can use these and bounce between them using your whip, to get an idea of what you're working with in this part.

In this upper section, from the purple anchors, jump onto the breakable platform and leap through the shards using your Halo. When you land on the second breakable platform, deactivate the Halo and wall leap from side to side across the shards.

When you get to the top, during a jump, activate the Halo and leap up to grab the purple anchor, deactivating the Halo for a final time when you've reached the top.

You've nearly cleared this section! In this section, you'll need to attach to the purple anchor to your far left, and leap over to the breakable platforms. Wall-leap on the left one, and jump up to the yellow anchor above you.

From there, swing up to the right side, and lash out with the whip to attach to the purple anchor on the right side, and you'll have cleared this part of the Collapsed Path of Orpheus!

You can make your way to the right through the glowing door and follow the path to the mysterious blue door at the end of the hallway.

Once through the hallway, you'll start a brief cutscene as Rose comes across the Ferryman, an associate of Death. He ferries the souls to Death, but does not work for him. After the cutscene, approach the brazier to interact with it, and you'll now be able to fast travel between sections that you unlock in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. It's a nifty fast travel method for you, and it unlocks another part that we'll cover shortly. Make your way to the Paris Streets and proceed through your playthrough.

When you've picked the Paris Streets, you'll return to this section of the map, but in an area you haven't been through yet. It's called the Justice District Sewers , and you'll need to proceed up to get out. Thankfully, you're not too far from your goal.

Jumping onto the platform above you, take either the left or right yellow anchor and swing to the center chamber, activating your Halo to bypass the shards. You'll then need to hoist yourself up from the purple anchors to reach the top, and then take the left pathway.

This will bring you to the Bridge of the Millers , a section you may have been to before in Paris Streets. Destroy the door blocking your path, connecting these two sections. Proceed to the left, defeat the fish enemy you encounter, and destroy the second door blocking your path to further connect these areas.

You'll find a lever on the other side that controls the rotating waterwheel. Have it rotate counterclockwise to bring you up, and you'll have reached topside where you can see Dracula's Castle in the distance. Rose has a quick moment to take it in, speaking with the various spirits trapped in her Tarot cards. Although Joan and Leon are supportive, Medusa further attempts to drive a wedge of doubt into Rose, reminding her of Dracula's Curse.

Still, Rose continues forward to face Dracula. Once this cutscene wraps up, follow the path to the right side, and head through the glowing door. This will bring you to the Court of Justice.

When entering the Justice District, take the yellow anchor above you and swing through the grate. You'll encounter a handful of undead that you need to dispatch before needing to make your way to the right.

In the upper area, you'll find a lower wall section that you can slide underneath and head below. Taking these grates down, you'll find a lever that you can hit to open both blocked pathways, connecting these sections. Proceed to the right, but stop at the door, and head through it.

Inside the room, on the left side, you'll discover a note left by Trevor. Here, he shares that he was unable to find the Bishop and asks that Rose find him immediately so the pair can investigate the town, while also warning her about going underground.

This is not the only note in this room. Before you leave, head to the right part of the doorway, and destroy the wall. Here, you'll find a piece of a diary, and this will unlock a Tarot card for Rose: the Miser, and give you an Arcana Clue about where you can find the Miser.

You'll want to note this for the future, but this won't bring you closer to Dracula's Castle, at least for now. Exit the building and proceed to the right path, going through the doorway. This brings you to the Docks.

Proceed down to the lower area of the docks, and you'll enter an enemy encounter ambush, pitting you against a Minotaur. It's a difficult elite enemy that can rush you from one side of this arena to the other. You can use the yellow anchors on the upper sections of this section to get out of the way.

When you're in close range, expect it to unleash heavy, wide poleaxe swings toward you. You can try to dodge underneath them, but it's tricky. You might be better off dodging out of the way, and staying away from these attacks, using your whip attack to close the distance, and landing heavy blows against it. Your ranged magic abilities are also a good choice here, too.

Once it's defeated, continue to the right and proceed to the next area known as the Gate to the Stone Bridge. Before heading up, I recommend making your way to the right and unlocking the Gate to the Stone Bridge Mirror of Life, using it as a checkpoint. Also, it's a good time to test out the new unlock that you get after meeting The Ferryman.

Now, if you have Rose crouch down in front of any Mirror of Life, this will take her to the Hall of Mirrors.

Here, you'll be able to bounce between specific Mirror of Life locations you've unlocked throughout your playthrough. You can use this as a quicker fast travel method, rather than relying on the Ferryman to take you between the larger districts, or by going there on foot. We recommend revisiting this location frequently throughout your time playing the game, unlocking the Hall of Mirrors further to make travel that much easier.

When you're ready to return to Paris through the Hall of Mirrors, crouch in front of any mirror, and you'll be transported through it and taken to your destination. You can return to the Gate of the Stone Bridge and return to your pathway on the left side, taking the route up.

Follow the pathway and staircase along this path, and when you reach the top, you'll arrive at the gate to Dracula's Castle. Hit the lever on the right, and proceed through, unlocking and activating the Main Hall.

You won't get too far on this path. As you reach the first jump, a conversation between Rose and Leon takes place, as Leon warns about Dracula's Curse on Rose's arm.

In this back-and-forth, Leon confirms his identity by revealing a closely guarded family secret to ensure he is truthfully saying who he is. Rose believes him, building their relationship further, before Medusa jumps in, cutting the conversation short. Here, you'll unlock the Main Hall section of Dracula's Castle, bringing you one step closer to bringing down the Lord of Darkness.

When the conversation is finished, make your way forward. You'll have to jump down to the lower section. Here, you'll find a lower platform where a fishman enemy pops up that you'll defeat before making your way up to the right side, taking the yellow and purple anchors to return to the upper section on the right side.

On the next platform, multiple undead will appear from the ground as you continue making your way to the right. Here, you'll encounter a new enemy, a knight with a lance. These enemies have extended range compared to the other melee undead and enemies you've encountered so far. They'll be able to hit you from farther away, and spin their polearms around them as they advance toward you.

When they're spinning the polearms, dodge out of the way and hit them from afar, using your magic attacks until the spinning stops. From there, try to use your whip attack to close the distance quickly and get a solid hit against them. They are tougher than the other enemies, especially if a pair of them show up.

In this part, a group of harpies also appears above you during this fight. One harpy in particular continues to spawn, but you can use them to reach the higher yellow anchor, before swinging with it to the right to clear the bridge and using the second yellow anchor to reach the other side.

When you're across the bridge, go to the covered section and use the grates to reach the lever, opposite the two purple anchors. Hit it, opening the blocked pathway to your right, and lowering the bridge to your left. This also activates the various enemies that you'll need to defeat before continuing to the right.

From here, follow the path to a lower area close to the water. There are small platforms you can jump on with gaps between them. Several fish foes appear from the water, along with harpies in the sky.

After dealing with them, proceed to the right, using the lower yellow anchor to swing to the right, and then to the left. Use the left swing to reach the higher yellow anchor, reaching the top area from here.

You'll find an enemy ambush waiting for you, as this section blocks your passage forward. You'll need to defeat the harpies that spawn, the polearm knights, and the large crow that appears. However, after defeating the large crow, the walls disappear, and you proceed forward. You can escape this section without defeating all of the polearm knights.

The right side leads to a boss door, and a showdown against those preventing you from crossing the bridge. You can use the purple anchor above you to find a hidden chicken in the wall, if you need healing, before proceeding forward.

As you proceed through the boss door, you'll encounter a notable pair of Count Dracula's servants: Carmilla and Isaac. These two welcome Rose as she arrives at the Castle, eager to stop her from entering the Castle. Although Carmilla retreats, Isaac remains behind to stop you from going forward.

When battling against Isaac, he teleports around the arena in an attempt to confuse you, utilizing his polearm to hit you from a distance. Both of these are telegraphed movements that you can use to your advantage. The teleport occurs as a green aura appears around Isaac, and before each of his polearm hits, Isaac raises his polearm behind him to swing out and forward.

There are three types of polearm attacks that Isaac does. There's a simple, close-range one that hits you in front of him. It's covered in green energy as he makes two swipes in front of himself. There's a larger one that's closer to the top of your head, and you can dodge this one by going underneath it. The third is a lower attack that's aimed at your lower body, and you can jump over this to avoid the attack.

Another attack Isaac uses happens when he floats in the air. He places his lance behind him, and it begins to float on its own. It will then begin spinning, seeking you out. The lance will haunt your footsteps as it races around the map to hit you, still seeking you out even if it lands an attack. The attack is brief, though, and Isaac will teleport to his lance and appear next to it.

You'll want to look out for when Isaac goes to the center of the arena and begins to spin his lance in front of him. Green shards begin to fly out from him, and cover the room in a pinwheel motion. The farther away from these attacks you are, the more they separate, providing an opening where you can go between them.

At the end of the fight, Isaac reveals that his form is an illusion. He's hiding somewhere in the Clock Tower, as Dracula builds up his strength once again. As Isaac leaves, the bridge of the Castle drops, inviting her inside.

Once inside, go through the Castle Garden, and then make your way to the Entrance Corridor in the Main Hall. Here, a conversation plays out as Rose steels herself to face off against Dracula. Joan and Leon believe in her, but warn her of Dracula's Curse and that she'll need to become stronger before she confronts him. If she does so too early, her curse can consume her, and she'll lose herself.

After this conversation happens, the other Tarot cards reveal their names, and you'll unlock all of them. You'll now need to work your way through these Tarot cards, with the first being The Builder. You won't find them in the Main Hall. Instead, for this next part of this playthrough, we'll be making our way through the Main Hall to the Clock Tower, and face off against The Builder.

Up Next: Clock Tower - Finding the Builder Walkthrough

articles.title: A Beginning Beyond the Waves Walkthrough - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Beginning Beyond the Waves is a Faction Quest that is part of the Charting the Unknown DLC category in Crimson Desert. This quick side quest has you sail for
articles.body:
A Beginning Beyond the Waves is a Faction Quest that is part of the Charting the Unknown DLC category in Crimson Desert . This quick side quest has you sail for the first time as you travel to an uncharted island southeast of Vellua. Follow our walkthrough for help sailing with the wind and to make sure you go to the right spot!

A Beginning Beyond the Waves Walkthrough

After completing the previous quest, Where the Wind Blows , you'll be out in the water ready to sail the ocean. As the helpful windows leading into this quest explain, your sails can lower and raise depending on where the wind is. Your goal is to sail with the wind to get the most speed on your way to the Auronui Island.

Across two trips from Vellua to Auronui Island, we've had the wind flow toward it. Therefore, as long as you watch the white streaks flowing through the air and sail with them , you'll move quickly. If you're having trouble seeing them, you can also look at your minimap near the bottom left corner . It'll now have a small icon that represents where the wind is coming from, while pointing to where it's going.

If you pass the island or are stuck sailing against the wind, you'll want to have your sails mostly raised. However, the Rigger crewman will prevent you from lowering them to a certain extent. If you're able to sail diagonally and zig-zag to your destination, that can help you catch the wind.

Aside from the wind mechanics, you may run into enemies as we did . Instead of battling pirate ships, we actually encountered Kite Pirates who glided onto our ship. You can either hop off the ship's wheel to fight them or leave it to your crew. With that said, this could have been a random event and may not happen to you.

Otherwise, all you have to do is sail close enough to Auronui to trigger a cutscene that will complete A Beginning Beyond the Waves. This then unlocks two new quests, Secret of the Winding Island and Footsteps in Unfamiliar Lands .

articles.title: Chronicles: Medieval Developer 'At Real Risk of Closing' Before Release as Funding 'No Longer in Place'
articles.summary: Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games posted a chilling warning on its social media pages, warning that the studio might close before it can launch the Early Access version of its medieval open-world action/strategy sandbox because funding for the team is "no longer in place."
articles.body:
Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games posted a chilling warning on its social media pages, warning that the studio might close before it can launch the Early Access version of its medieval open-world action/strategy sandbox because funding for the team is "no longer in place."

In a message on X (with a hat tip to Insider Gaming ), Raw Power laid out its unfortunate predicament: "Due to circumstances outside our control, the necessary funding behind Raw Power Games is no longer in place. Without it we can't keep building Chronicles: Medieval, and right now the studio is at real risk of closing. We're not going to sugarcoat. You deserve to hear it plainly, and directly from us.

"What makes it hurt is how close we are," the message continued. "Early Access is within reach. The world we've been building for years is finally starting to feel alive, and we have so much we've been thrilled to show you. Every day in the studio – in Copenhagen and remote – we've seen people put everything they have into this game, often far beyond what anyone asked of them. They are the ones carrying the heaviest weight right now, and we couldn't be prouder of them. We don't know yet how this ends. But in the spirit of our game we're not going down without a fight!"

Chronicles: Medieval's Tom Hardy-narrated announcement trailer drew a lot of interest, netting more than 2 million views on IGN's YouTube channel . It was revealed at Summer Game Fest 2025, and we have since previewed it not once but twice . In our most recent hands-on, we noted that it still felt pretty early at the time, but also said, "The scale and detail of the battles simultaneously is very impressive," and, "Being able to jump into a commander at ground level for more of a third-person action mode is really cool."

Raw Power Games told fans, "If you want to stand with us, keep Chronicles: Medieval on your wishlist and keep talking about it. It matters more right now than you might think. Thank you for believing in us. Thank you for believing in this game. We really hope you'll get to play the world we've been creating."

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Final Fantasy XIV Evercold Delayed, New Release Date Announced at FFXIV Fan Fest
articles.summary: The MMORPG's next expansion was set to launch shortly after the new year, but Warriors of Light will have to wait a bit longer.
articles.body:
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold was set to launch sometime in January 2027, which was announced as part of its initial reveal back in April this year during the North American FFXIV Fan Fest. However, this next expansion for the critically acclaimed MMORPG has been delayed – FFXIV Evercold's release date is now February 23, 2027 (and February 19, 2027 for early access). This was announced alongside the new, full trailer / intro cinematic for Evercold at FFXIV Fan Fest in Japan, and was said to only be a four-week delay.

In typical FFXIV fashion, the third and final teaser trailer is the full opening cinematic for an expansion, and it kicked off the Japan Fan Fest keynote where director and producer Naoki Yoshida presented more details on new features, where the ongoing story is headed, and fundemental gameplay changes as FFXIV goes into version 8.0 alongside Evercold's launch.

Pre-orders for Evercold open on November 4, 2026 and will come with several bonus items, which will be revealed later in the Fan Fest keynote - I will update this as they are shown. Additionally, we got a glimpse of the second new Job coming to his new expansion. It's a ranged DPS called Zephyr, which rocks a crossbow as their primary weapon and commands an avian companion to provide support.

There's a lot coming to FFXIV Evercold in addition to a new world and main story including a Neon Genesis Evangelion crossover raid series , a Final Fantasy VII crossover raid series, a new Tank Job with Bastion, and much more. Be sure to check out my Dawntrail review as well to look back at the last expansion before heading into this new era for FFXIV.

articles.title: Arkade is a PC Peripheral That Transforms Every Modern Shooter Into a Light Gun Game
articles.summary: Arkade is a PC Peripheral That Transforms Every Modern Shooter Into a Light Gun Game
articles.body:
If you miss the days of Time Crisis, Virtua Cop, or even Duck Hunt, then Arkade Gaming Gun is a PC peripheral that should be firmly in your sights. At this week’s Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show 2026, I managed to get a short hands-on demonstration with this motion-controlled gun controller that’s due to release sometime in 2027 and came away with a strong first impression despite taking a few moments to wrap my head around its unique control setup.

What’s great about the Arkade Gaming Gun straight off the bat is that its proprietary technology doesn’t require a webcam or Wii-style sensor bar to make it work with your display. It’s completely plug and play, you connect its charging dock up to your PC via USB-C, and it doubles as a wireless receiver for the gun itself. A device manager allows you to customise its button layout and calibrate the tracking performance, and away you go.

You basically cradle the Arkade in a two-handed grip. The D-Pad or WASD-style movement of your character is handled by a thumbstick jutting out the side of its chunky barrel – which pulses with customisable LED graphics like a billboard in a Blade Runner skyline – with a pair of buttons on the other side used for other moves like jumping, and controls at the rear for weapon-switching.

Otherwise the actual aiming is handled by physically pointing the gun itself at your target, and that’s where things became initially disorientating during my brief hands-on. Dropped into a demo of Prodeus, a boomer shooter from developer Bounding Box Software, it took a moment for me to get comfortable with strafing and aiming at the same time. This was largely because to activate the aiming ability of Arkade you need to lightly grip the capacitive touch surface of its trigger. Rest your finger on the trigger and the onscreen crosshair will move to whatever target that you aim the gun at. Take your finger off the trigger, however, and you’re basically locked in the direction that you’re facing, as though you were playing with a mouse and keyboard and suddenly slipped your hand off the mouse.

Once I did get a feel for it, though, it largely became second nature. I even started instinctively re-centring myself on the fly with subtle movements of my trigger finger, not unlike when you’re aiming with a mouse and you’re pushing towards the edge of the mouse pad, and you pick it up and place it back in the middle without really thinking about it. It’s a fairly tricky thing to explain, but basically once it clicks it feels incredibly fun to peer down the Arkade’s sights and blaze away at a room of Doom-style demons with no noticeable compromises to the freedom of your movements. I especially like how its trigger features two stages of operation – a half-squeeze basically mimics a right mouse-button by zooming in slightly on your target, while a full squeeze fires the shot.

According to its creator and CEO Joshua Fuchs, the Arkade Gaming Gun isn’t solely designed for first-person shooters. Apparently it also supports a number of third-person shooters as well, from Fortnite to the Resident Evil 3 remake. It can also be used in conjunction with other peripherals to further increase the immersion, with Fuchs showing me a video example of one of his team members using the Arkade Gaming Gun in tandem with a racing wheel to execute drive-by shootings in Grand Theft Auto 5; one hand on the wheel and the other pulling the trigger on the Arkade. I’m not sure how much peripheral-juggling and custom controller-mapping would be required to play the entire game that way, but it certainly suggested that players could have a lot of fun getting creative with this device.

For now the Arkade gaming gun only supports PC, Mac, and Steam OS, but Fuchs has hopes of bringing it to consoles at some point in the future. The gun itself feels really solidly constructed, but light enough that I don’t imagine it would become too tiring to wield it for extended gaming sessions.

One thing that does feel a little heavy though, is the price. Arkade Gaming Gun is launching at $399 USD, although there is currently the option of scoring one at a discounted rate if you preorder from Arkade’s website . That’s a fairly hefty price to pay to bring a feeling of old school nostalgia to new school shooting, but if you’ve got the budget for it then based on my brief blast with it this light gun feels like it could be worth a shot.

Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video editor at IGN based in Sydney, Australia. He has 25 years of experience covering video games, having served as Deputy Editor on Official PlayStation 2 Magazine Australia and as Editor of Official Xbox 360 Magazine Australia, before joining IGN in 2009. You can find him on Bluesky @tristanogilvie.bsky.social

Footsteps in Unfamiliar Lands Walkthrough

After completing the previous quest, A Beginning Beyond the Waves , you'll have made it to Auronui Island. This quest revolves around a new pioneering system that allows you to capture uncharted islands. Unfortunately, at the time of the DLC's release, it's been broken for a lot of players. Then, you can assign three Deckhands from your ship if you brought them on board at a Ship Manager. You'll also need the following resources ot complete the Pioneer dispatch:
