articles.title: The Saw Turns Again Walkthrough - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Saw Turns Again is a Faction Quest that is part of the Charting the Unknown DLC category in Crimson Desert. This side quest teaches you how to run your
articles.body:
The Saw Turns Again is a Faction Quest that is part of the Charting the Unknown DLC category in Crimson Desert . This side quest teaches you how to run your first Facility, while also unlocking other ones across Pywel to eventually lease. Follow our walkthrough to start generating Camp Funds for the greymanes! We've included helpful info on how to level up your popularity and how to get the recipes you'll need here.

After completing the previous quest, The Stilled Saw, you'll have learned that the Timberham Sawmill is available to lease. First, find the Timberham Sawmill on your map . It's south-southwest of the Town of Hernand, not too far away. This places it across from the Capra Pasture.

Once you've found it, switch to the Facilities filter on your map. This will show you the sawmill, allowing you to inspect it and then lease it . As long as you have 15,000 Camp Funds via the Greymanes, you'll be able to lease the property. Next, travel over if you're not already there.

Enter the Management Mode at the Sawmill

Upon entering the sawmill, you'll get a tooltip that explains how to open the Management menu. This leads to more helpful information that walks you through managing the sawmill to get it up and running. After entering the Management menu, tap on the Manage Staff button.

On this screen, you can assign two Greymanes to the Carpenter role and one to the Sawyer role . You'll likely want to have more comrades available to assign as new slots open up. However, this is enough to get you started. While you can employ anyone in these roles, you'll receive bonuses for putting Crafters on Carpenter and Loggers on Sawyer.

As far as Camp Fund upkeep goes for each employee, don't worry about that. The sawmill will offset the upkeep as long as you don't overprice your goods and scare off customers. Once you've finished assigning staff, return to the previous menu and press Open Shop. Now you'll need to wait for customers to buy enough goods until you reach Popularity level 1.

As you level up your Facility's popularity, you'll have to complete specific goals to reach higher levels. For the Timberham Sawmill, you'll need to fulfill the following objectives to reach level 2:

You'll need to read the book, The Courtesy of Waiting, to learn the Waiting Table recipe that the quest refers to as a Standing Table. Reaching Popularity level 1 gives you the book as a reward. After doing so, head back to the Management menu and tap on the Place Installables button. Check the bottom right corner for the button prompt to open your Installables inventory.

Under the section that has an icon of a building and a chest, you'll find the Standing Table all the way to the right. You'll need at least 2,000 Camp Funds to place one inside the sawmill. After doing so, return to the previous menu and tap on Manage Goods. Now that you're at Popularity Lvl. 1, you'll have an extra slot for a second item to sell.

By default, you should have the Wood synergy task complete if you kept the default good here. Otherwise, you can select one with the Wood tag beneath its name. Adding a second item with the Wood tag will increase the synergy bonus. Then, as long as you keep the Selling Price bar in the green for a Favorable response, you'll satisfy three customers easily.

Similar to the previous level, follow the new tasks to reach level 3 popularity. These include the following:

Place a plank workbench (Crude Plank Workbench)

Reading the previous book mentioned will teach you the recipes for a Crude Plank Workbench and Crude Plank Box. Place them inside your sawmill to complete those tasks and to unlock plank goods. Afterward, return to the Manage Goods area in the Management mode. Pick three goods with the Plank tag so you can easily finish the task of selling 10 plank goods.

Upon reaching Popularity level 3, you'll have completed The Saw Turns Again. You can continue working on tasks to get other rewards and to make more money at your Facility. Or you can let it run on its own as you wander Pywel.

articles.title: Deep In The Valley - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Deep In The Valley is one of the first optional Purple Story Quests in Phantom Blade Zero you can actually complete.
articles.body:
Deep In The Valley is one of the first optional Purple Story Quests in Phantom Blade Zero you can actually complete.

Starting this quest is fairly easy. After you defeat Peng Meng , you will progress forwards, eventually completing the chapter. You will then make your way to the Sha-Chi Tower. Just next to the Creek Valley Plains Entrance bell, the nearby disciple tells you he dropped the base camp gate key inside the Steel Tower while escaping faceless enemies. This begins the Deep in the Valley purple quest.

Here are the steps to complete the quest:

Before you can collect the Base Camp Gate key, you need to find the Hunter's Chain Sickle. This is dropped upon defeating The Hunt, Hunter of the Order at the very end of the Weeping Creek Valley area.

Therefore, progress onwards until you defeat The Hunt. A full breakdown of the boss guide is below:

Some of his moves should feel familiar, but here are the special attacks you need to look out for:

The Hunt can attack from most ranges with wild chain sickle moves. Parrying will lower his Sha-Chi meter quickly, but if you’re not confident in the timings, just block until you see a blue or red flash attack. And switch weapons defensively to refill your Sha-Chi meter if it runs low while blocking.

Offensively, you can overwhelm the Hunt, especially if you obtained the Scarlet Wraithblade from the optional boss battle against Hua, Deadly Betrothed . It creates patches of Red Spider Lilies that drain the Hunt’s health if he stands in them during both Sha-Chi combos and Power Surges. And sometimes, a button prompt pops up during longer combos, giving you chances to deal extra damage.

The Hunt regains all of his HP once you fully deplete his health bar. This is phase two, against The Hunt, Sixfold Scythe . He now has extra arms that come with new attacks, so here are all of the new special moves that you should watch out for.

The Hunt has more arms in this phase, which means he has more sickles to launch your way. The attacks are a bit quicker and can hit you from a greater distance. He also has a slow-moving projectile that hits multiple times.

Your strategy doesn’t need to change much offensively – you can still overwhelm the boss. Just try not to overextend your combos, especially when you see the Hunt’s Sha-Chi meter refill.

You’re rewarded with the Hunter’s Chain Sickle Phantom Edge which is needed for this fight.

With the Hunter's Chain Sickle, you want to travel back to the Sha-Chi Tower and climb to its peak. Here you will meet the Watchful Shadow Warden, which is a part of the A Severed Mindseal Tale side quest.

But, just to the right, you can find a wall to climb up and then a pipe to walk across.

At the end you can use the Hunter's Chain Sickle to jump up to the higher part of the tower.

Sitting here is the Sha-Chi Tower Base Camp Gate Key.

With the Base Camp Gate Key, return to the Creek Valley Plains Entrance bell and open the gate next to it.

This opens up an entirely optional area to explore allowing you to complete other side quests like Four Fierce Axes , Apprentice Healer , and Bloodline Awakening . This will also complete this quest.

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Showrunners Address Your Biggest Finale Burning Questions
articles.summary: Avatar: Seven Havens: We talk with show co-creator Michael Dante DiMartino and showrunners Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding about the current season and beyond.
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for Avatar: Seven Havens Season 1!

The first Book of Avatar: Seven Havens is, er, in the books with this week’s finale, “The Root Chakra.” And while the final four episodes answered a number of big questions, they raised a ton more — not just about what to expect in Season 2 of the Paramount+ animated series, but Seasons 3, 4, and perhaps beyond. It’s a good thing, then, that we have show co-creator Michael Dante DiMartino and showrunners Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding on hand to answer all your burning questions.

…Or at least, answer what they can . While we got to see Pavi (Saheli Khan) step up as the Avatar in the finale, unlock her Root Chakra, and head off on a classic Avatar journey to the Floating Isles next season, Nisha (Aishu Devan) — surprisingly — was not part of that unlocking and is staying (for now) in the Haven of Ellora. Not only that, but we also saw Nisha was at least in part the cause of the Fear Anomaly that’s been attacking Ellora all season long, activated when her parents abandoned her; as a side effect, she accidentally killed her parents in a rock slide.

But there are still the questions of why and how Avatar Korra caused a Cataclysm 225 years earlier, how there are twin Avatars now, and many more mysteries and surprises to explore. So let’s get into it and see what DiMartino, Sethi, and Spaulding can answer about the future of the Avatar franchise.

Before we get to that, though, earlier this week the world of animation suffered a shocking loss with the passing of actor Eric Bauza at age 46. Bauza voiced multiple characters in this season of Seven Havens, and given the pace of animation, we’ll likely hear his voice for several seasons to come. But his passing does leave a huge gap in the world of Avatar.

“Eric meant a lot, obviously, to the show,” Spaulding said. “He's all over Seven Havens, and his contribution to animation in general is so prevalent. He's going to leave a big hole.” Sethi continued, “He worked on this show, but we all have history with him beyond this show. He's worked on so many things. I joked all the time that Bauza was twenty percent of the population of Seven Havens. We used him because he was so brilliant. He could act against himself. He could do young, old, any voice you could think of… Every single time he was in that booth, he was an absolute delight… He was just the kindest person… It's just the biggest loss.”

But Bauza’s contributions stretch beyond Seven Havens.

“He was actually in Avatar: The Last Airbender,” DiMartino recalled. “That was when he was just getting started in his voice-acting career. I think he's like a guard or two in the Boiling Rock. So the fact that he's been part of this universe for so long… I knew he was a big deal, [but] hearing all the stories from people over the past week, just learning more about him and the impact he's had on the community and everyone he's worked with is, it's just very sad. And [we] wish his family the best.”

To get into the show itself, it’s a surprise that Pavi heads off on the classic Avatar journey at the end of the season alongside airbender Jae (Major Curda) while Nisha stays behind in Ellora. That, of course, was always part of the plan.

“From the very beginning, we all wanted this to be a really organic story about two sisters,” Sethi said. “Yes, there's a lot of world-building. There's so much that's going on. But at the end of the day, they are two young girls who fight and have differing opinions. Now that we've spent a whole Book, a whole season, seeing them grow together… What is it going to be like now when they're apart? How are they going to grow apart from one another into their respective roles? That was really interesting to me.”

Added Spaulding, “Also, getting the characters out into the world so the audience can see… other locations, it's a cool thing to have the characters split up at some point in the storyline for the world-building.”

Part of that world-building is the next Haven Pavi is headed towards: The Floating Isles. We’re told she senses trouble there, and it seems likely that’s the location of the next Chakra she needs to unlock. So what can they tell us about the place?

Not much. “That's Haven Number Two, and Pavi will be visiting there,” DiMartino confirmed. Calling it a “more chill place compared to Ellora,” which was greeted by knowing laughter from Spauling and Sethi, DiMartino continued, “It's definitely a different vibe culturally. We try to make every Haven they're going to visit its own mini-culture [with] different customs and everything. So it'll be fun to start seeing more of the world as we get out there.”

There Will Be More Than One Haven Per Season

Given Book 1 was entirely in Ellora, one might venture that Book 2 will be entirely in the Floating Isles. This would mean that either the show is going seven seasons or we’re going to go a little faster than we did in Season 1; turns out, it’s the latter.

“No, not exactly,” DiMartino said when asked about the ‘one Haven per season’ idea. “We had to split it up a little differently, but we'll get through all the Seven Havens by the end of this series for sure.”

Beyond that, they confirmed that the four seasons of the show is the entire series. “That’s the full story,” DiMartino said. Added Sethi, “When Mike, Bryan [Konietzko], and I started working on it, we always had an end goal in mind — a lighthouse for us to work the story towards — and that's always been the case throughout the series.”

Apologies in advance, because the answer to this one won’t be satisfying, but we did ask about the revelation that Pavi’s chakras are messed up and she is able to unlock the Root Chakra alone but not with Nisha. So is repairing the Cataclysm solely up to Pavi? Is she the “real” Avatar, and is Nisha a side effect or something else?

“We’ll see,” Sethi said enigmatically. “You gotta keep watching, man. I promise all of those questions are answered.”

One of the darkest moments in Avatar history is when it’s revealed that not only did Nisha’s parents abandon her, but in the process of summoning the Fear Anomaly, she accidentally killed them in a rock slide. While Sethi confirmed that there’s more to this story to come, it’s still a horrifying duo of revelations that skew way darker than fans were likely expecting.

“I don't want to speak for Mike or Ethan, but when we started the series, I always had a feeling this is going to be darker,” Sethi said. ”We were really tackling some difficult and complex situations. The amount of power these girls wield… I always was interested in the idea of putting very young characters in very mature positions. I thought there was something really interesting there, especially from a storytelling point of view. We're really forcing the girls to grow up in a lot of ways, and so for me that was just an interesting place to go as a storyteller. For the show and for where we are taking the story, it made sense to start dividing the girls on not just a philosophical level but an emotional level, and this is the biggest emotional divide you can give two characters. So to me, I really wanted to explore that in the upcoming season.”

Added DiMartino, “In the early development that Bryan and I did, we had [the] idea of this tragic backstory that happened with Nisha, the family, and Pavi. That's how she lost her leg. So the core of that ended up being what's in the show. We always knew that was going to be a big part of the mystery of Book One and a big reveal, and like you said, it's a dark moment. But it's totally necessary for their characters and the story, and so it all ties together. And yeah, there's more that we will dig into around that story in upcoming seasons.”

During a climactic moment in the finale when Pavi unlocks the Root Chakra, she also sees a vision of four past Avatars: Kyoshi, Aang, Roku, and finally, Korra. While Spaulding explained this is a nod to the constellation versions of the Avatars seen previously in both The Last Airbender and Legend of Korra, there seems to be a little more to it. And no, it’s not Pavi reconnecting with the Avatar Cycle after Korra broke the connection towards the end of Legend of Korra.

“It’s something else,” said DiMartino. “She has not reconnected. It can't happen that easily. So she does have a connection with Korra, but the other stuff's more of a vision.”

Added Sethi, “That's something we really had to work [on showing] visually that the connection is not complete. It was not just, oh, let's show Korra for a second or something. It was like, hey, she's sort of faded, right? She's not completely there. We wanted it to not just be so easy as, yup, now Korra can talk to you. That's something that still needs to progress in the series.”

Fans did notice in earlier episodes that both Korra and Asami are wearing betrothal necklaces in a “mover,” while in a vision of Korra where she’s tearing down Republic City, she is not. So how worried do we need to be about Asami?

“Asami is definitely dead by our show, which I think is a fair thing to say.” Sethi said. “The main thing to know from that is that there is most likely a time jump. But as to their relationship, you do learn more about that in Season 2.”

More LGBTQ+ Relationships in Seven Havens

One huge leap forward for the franchise is the amount of LGBTQ+ representation on screen. The final episode of Legend of Korra pretty famously had some issues in showing Korra and Asami getting together back in 2014. In 2026? Not only are the duo clearly together (and maybe betrothed), but we’ve also followed a canonically gay couple in Jae and Datu (Topher Ngu), and at least one other female-female pairing has shown up on screen.

“I definitely think that TV [and] even the kids’ animation landscape has definitely changed,” DiMartino reflected. “Whereas on Korra, we ran into some… pushback about what we could and couldn't show, this time around everyone was super supportive and it's more about the storytelling. What is the best way to show these relationships? It's nice to see, and we will see more of what Korra and Asami's relationship was like in the past.”

Despite Pavi unlocking the Root Chakra, things aren’t quite settled in Ellora, particularly since Chancellor Kayoko (Jennifer Sun Bell) is still clearly possessed by the Fear Anomaly as the season ends. So what’s going on here? Is the Root Chakra still blocked?

“The afflicted stay afflicted until a certain point,” Spaulding explained. “So there's still something that the Avatar has to do.”

Added Sethi, “Yeah, their journey is not finished with just releasing that energy. There's more that they'll need to do.”

We’re Not Getting a Huge Time Jump (Probably [Yet])

Fans at New York Comic Con noticed some designs of Pavi and Nisha that seemed to depict their characters aged up significantly, but as Sethi clarified, “that was concept art. So whether there's a time jump, who's to say, but that was not a time jump piece of art. That was just concept art.”

Other than that, though, time will be progressing forward as it tends to do. “Within the span of a series, there's time in between episodes,” Spaulding explained. “It's not very big, but you could say they're traveling for weeks or months. It’s similar to Last Airbender.”

“Yeah, now that they're on the road, [you] gotta account for the travel time in certain ways,” DiMartino added. “Time passes, but it's not like we're jumping forward years or anything.”

Instead, they’re letting the growing maturity of the characters come from subtle animation changes, like a loosening of Pavi’s hair in the finale and the vocal performances of the actresses.

“I give so much credit to Saheli, who plays Pavi, and Aishu, who plays Nisha,” Sethi said. “I give those amazing young ladies so much credit that they really learned how to grow their performance as the characters got more complex. They did a great job, and shout out to our amazing voice director Kristi Reed, who helped them with that.”

One of the fun parts of Seven Havens has been picking out post-apocalypse tropes hidden between the Avatar easter eggs. From a Mad Max-style introduction to two other Havens, to a zombie movie-esque Afflicted infestation, the series has embraced the setting in a big way. And while Sethi conceded they don’t have a list of tropes (or movies) they’re trying to hit, it is very much baked into the premise.

“The thing that I always found interesting when Mike and Bryan brought me this idea was that it's almost like post-post-apocalypse,” Sethi said. “They've created a new city, right? They've essentially already done the work of rebuilding, and now it's almost like, oh, is there another impending apocalypse coming? So that was the interesting thing of [doing] some post-apocalypse stuff, but it can't feel like Scavengers Reign because they've rebuilt. There are new places. We tried to weave it in where it really made logical sense with where the story was going and where the world was.”

Added DiMartino, “When you get into Book Two, though, and now that they're traveling, you're going to see more of the Harshlands and stuff. So that gives you more of the post-apocalyptic vibe, and why people aren't living out in these areas.”

Despite the multi-year schedule of creating animation, Seven Havens has felt laudably and eerily relevant to our world today. Turns of phrase in the finale like “We can’t just hide from the scary bubble” and “freedom of choice is all I’ve ever wanted” work on multiple levels. So how does a staff aiming for a hopefully timeless children’s animated series also reflect what we’re feeling right now in 2026?

“In a lot of ways, we were trying to really uphold an ethos that a lot of the Avatar world has always upheld,” Sethi explained. “I don't know if it's us getting political or everything that is relevant about humanity just being political at this point. To be truly honest, these were things that we always wanted to talk about, and we always felt they were timeless. We just happen to be in a time where they are incredibly relevant now.”

Added DiMartino, “All the Avatar stuff we've done has some political bent to it, but we're trying to address themes that are pervasive throughout history, not just talking about the current political climate. These are things that societies and people have struggled with throughout civilization’s history.”

“For me, especially, the idea of fear of the other, freedom of choice,” Sethi continued. “These are things that absolutely matter and will always matter. Like Mike was saying, the fact that they matter right now… Honestly, it's kind of cool that people can watch our show and feel a relevance now. But even 20 years from now, I think they'll still feel that relevance.”

The Hardest Part of Writing Seven Havens

Now that the secret of the show is out — that each of the Seven Havens does indeed align with one of the Seven Chakras — it gives the story a very clear, mission-based structure. But what it also does is somewhat dictate where Pavi and Nisha need to go emotionally over the course of the four seasons. So how do the writers balance honoring the emotional truth of those character’s journeys versus “well, we’ve gotta hit this chakra next.”

“Dude,” Sethi said, groaning. “That was the hardest part of the show. Truly, it was a massive undertaking. We did everything we could to make sure that their journeys would align with the world but would also align with them personally as organic characters. This is the hardest show I've ever worked on, and in the room, that was something that we went over and over. We probably tried like 17 different storylines because we wanted to make sure that the one we hit matched the characters as well as this overarching concept. So yeah, the best thing I can say is: It was really hard.”

Added DiMartino, “It's nice to have a structure [for] what we're going to be dealing with thematically. But then you have to honor that and also the characters we have. The thing I was excited about doing, now that we can talk about all the chakras stuff, is that the Guru was one of the people's favorite episodes from Avatar: The Last Airbender. But we had to cruise through the chakras real fast, so when we were revisiting that idea and the series, it was like, oh, this would be cool that we could structure the entire series and really explore these themes and make it not so easy to to unlock all of them. [We made] that the main journey of what Pavi has to go on.”

The Future of the Avatar Franchise From Seven Havens to Wave of Chaos and Beyond

There’s a lot coming in the future of Avatar, including three more seasons of Seven Havens, a new series titled Avatar Kuruk: Wave Of Chaos , and potentially more TBA. So let’s check in on what’s even further down the road than Season 2.

On Where They Are in Seven Havens: “ We've been working on this stuff for several years now, so we are deep into Books Three and Four,” DiMartino said. “And yeah, it'll be a little bit before they come out, but rest assured, it’s all being worked on.”

Will Seven Havens and Wave of Chaos Overlap on the Release Schedule? “That is beyond my scope of control,” DiMartino said, laughing. “So it'll depend on what Paramount Plus wants to do, I guess, or whatever the streaming app happens to be at that time. That's just getting started. It might be a bit before we have episodes ready for that.”

Will There Be Further Avatar Shows? How About Movies? “Potentially,” DiMartino said. “I mean, we've got ideas for other Avatar things. We can come up with ideas all day, but we need the higher-ups to greenlight stuff.”

You hear that, Paramount? Start clicking that green light button, because we need more Avatar in our lives!

articles.title: Aliens, Bigfoots, and Monsters… Remembering the Age of the Weirdumentary
articles.summary: In the conspiracy-minded 1970s, monster ‘documentaries’ were a huge hit at the box office.
articles.body:
“Scientists representing the world’s foremost research centers took part in the examination of the evidence. The facts that will be presented are true. This may be the most startling film you’ll ever see.” -Peter Graves, The Mysterious Monsters (1975)

During the turbulent era of Vietnam and Watergate, the happy veneer of America in the 1950s and ‘60s gave way to the conspiracy-minded ‘70s. Dark revelations about the government, justice system, military, and police made the public begin to rethink their perceptions about a great many things. This led to renewed interest in occult matters like ESP, UFOs, and cryptozoology. These subjects, along with other pseudoscientific phenomena like near-death experiences or the Bermuda Triangle, became the bread and butter of a Utah-based production house called Sunn Classic Pictures. The company made a fortune releasing partially-dramatized “documentaries” that tantalized viewers with possibilities of what could be out there beyond the veil.

“I think it was people just questioning what the norm was… what is real, what isn't real,” James L. Conway, who worked as a writer/producer/director at Sunn Classic, tells IGN. “There were very few outlets back then to experience these things, very few TV channels. Through a theatrical window, we were able to make movies about these subjects. They were incredibly popular because there was no other place for people to get knowledge about this… no YouTube, no Wikipedia, no social media. If you wanted to see something that was on the unusual side, it was a theatrical motion picture.”

Conway was a college senior at the University of Denver around 1971 when he was in the Mass Communications Department and the phone rang. It was Charles E. Sellier Jr., who ran an industrial film and commercial company in Denver.

Continues Conway, “Chuck was looking for cheap labor to edit his industrial films. I said, ‘I'm your guy.’ While I finished college I worked for Chuck, and after about three months I said to him, ‘You know, I can direct these shows better than the people you're hiring.’ Total chutzpah. He gave me a shot, I did really well, and that began our relationship.”

After producing a western comedy called The Brothers O'Toole, Sellier connected with Sunn Classic Pictures, which at that point was a distribution outfit in Utah and a newly-founded division of the Schick razor company. They had made several well-attended hunting pictures like The Life and Times of Grizzly Adams, and decided their next avenue would be a series of pseudoscience documentaries kicked off by a re-edited and English dubbed version of the 1970 German doc Chariots of the Gods . Based on Erich von Däniken’s popular claptrap supposing celestial beings who seeded early humanity, in 1973 it grossed over $25M and was nominated for an Oscar.

Noted film scholar Dr. Gary D. Rhodes recently published a book titled Weirdumentary all about this era of strange docs throughout the ‘70s, of which he claims Chariots of the Gods is the urtext: “The fact that it was nominated for an Academy Award suggests how many more people were taking these ideas seriously. I hesitate to think a documentary on that subject now would get an Academy Award nomination. From the late ‘60s we see a rise in interest in everything from occultism and psychic phenomena, new age philosophies, magic, astrology, paganism, life after death, anti-materialism, holistic medicine, reincarnation… there's a desire to find alternate ways of examining our experiences that is unique to that era, including academia. You would not find many parapsychology departments in today's world.”

Once they found the winning formula, Sunn Classic released a wave of documentaries including 1975’s The Mysterious Monsters, where Mission: Impossible actor Peter Graves hosts a Whitman’s Sampler of cryptids.

“For me as a little kid, I certainly loved Mysterious Monsters the most of any of them because it was the era of fascination with Bigfoot, widespread belief that there might be such a creature,” says Rhodes. “There was equal interest in the Loch Ness monster and the Yeti. There were documentary films individually about all of those monsters, but here it was like the Universal monster rally films where you were getting all of them at once.”

The film was actually an amalgam of a few previously-released TV documentaries including CBS’ Monsters! Mystery or Myth, which helped popularize the supposed veracity of the Roger Patterson/Robert Gimlin footage of Bigfoot strolling through the woods. Narrates Graves, “If this film is legitimate, then there can no longer be any question about Bigfoot’s existence.”

Because Sunn Classic was a Mormon-run company, Rhodes says they “wanted to tap into films where everybody from a little kid to the grandparents could go and not feel out of place or offended.” Sellier himself called this demographic “the lost audience” who felt left behind by both the kiddie fare of Disney and the blood-and-nudity-soaked visions of New Hollywood auteurs (Taxi Driver, The Exorcist, etc.). Sunn’s product even included a few movies which attempted to present scientific evidence for aspects of the Christian faith. The most successful was In Search of Noah’s Ark, co-written and directed by Conway based on a book by Sellier and David W. Balsiger. It posits that (conveniently inaccessible) evidence exists that the remains of Noah's Ark lay on Turkey’s Mount Ararat. It includes several non-Russell Crowe re-enactments, as well as a supposed photograph that became the lynchpin for “proof.”

Intones narrator Brad Crandall, “The answer came in late September of 1974 when an expedition from the Holy Ground Mission in Frankston, Texas, scaled Mount Ararat, shooting across the Ahora Gorge with a 35MM Minolta camera. They took this picture that shows what looks like the fore part of a great vessel. The prow can be seen sticking out of the rocks 2000 feet above the location of the Eryl Cummings photo. When studied under photographic enlargement, the outline of the ship is not only clear but planking can actually be seen… the planking of Noah's Ark.”

“We didn't doctor anything… we had a photo that had been in other pieces of research,” Conway explained to us. “In those days, every expert you go to has their own data to support what they believe. Whether it's pseudoscience or not, all these people had books or research they could point to proving their point. A lot of it is things people wanted to believe, and so they'll accept the research more readily than a scientist might. I actually just saw there was a report on the Today Show last week about how they found this thing near Mount Ararat that they think is Noah's Ark. It just never goes away.”

Adds Rhodes of the questionable flood geology, “There's something atop Mount Ararat, and we think it's wood, and then this one explorer went up and claims to have seen it, and another explorer got close, but he couldn't quite get there. For some people, that's still tantalizing.”

Sunn Classics had several innovations to make and market their movies. They would often spend tens of thousands doing market research on whether a subject was viable for public interest. Once a film was complete, they would circumvent Hollywood distribution through a practice known as four-walling.

Conway claims that when Sunn approached local theaters, “They’d say, ‘We're going to pay you $25 cash for Friday night, $25 cash for Saturday night. We control the box office. Everything that comes in is ours.’ Because it was four-walled we did very heavy television commercials. We would only have, let's say, 300 prints of the movie. It would go into a city like Chicago, play two nights at this one theater, three nights at a different theater, four nights at another theater, and the commercials would list all the different movie theaters it was going to be on each night. They were enormously successful. On In Search of Noah's Ark I think our budget was $600,000 and it grossed $55 million. It was the 9th highest grossing movie of 1976.”

“Four-walling was a brilliant strategy,” opines Rhodes. “Sunn Classic were, in some respects, using old tricks of the trade not unlike the roadshow cinema of the early 20th century. In other respects, they were way ahead of their time. They were using surveys, polling at shopping malls: ‘What kind of film do you want to watch?’ They would look at advance weather reports in tandem with four-walling to try and avoid a snowstorm in the weeks ahead.”

“It may start in the Bible Belt, but it was huge everywhere you went,” continues Conway. “It was a huge hit, quite remarkable. That taught us that if you have a great commercial hook you can get a great box office return. That's where a lot of the supernatural elements come in, because there was an appetite for it. It's very easy to do a 15- or 20-second hook in a commercial to get people's interests up. It was so successful that theater runners made us go back to the standard splitting the box office, which was bad for us, good for them.”

Another “bad for us, good for them” was producer Alan Landsburg bringing the formula to television with an In Search of… docuseries hosted by Leonard Nimoy from 1976 to 1982. Landsburg helped popularize the style with the earlier docs In Search of Ancient Astronauts (1973), In Search of Ancient Mysteries (1974), and The Outer Space Connection (1975), the latter made and released by Sunn Classic. The show’s subjects (Extraterrestrials, Magic & Witchcraft, Missing Persons, Myths & Monsters, Lost Civilizations, Special Phenomena) were the same as Sunn’s, as was the format of a celebrity host.

“He came after us with the In Search of… television series, basically ripped off our In Search of Historic Jesus and In Search of Noah's Ark,” says Conway. “He made it a TV series that was very successful, but that came after we had done our stuff.”

Many others were tapping into the same material, including the Oscar-winning insectsploitation doc The Hellstrom Chronicle (1971) and the Rod Serling-hosted UFOs: Past, Present, and Future (1974), but Rhodes says that “Sunn Classic was at the core of the weirdumentary.” The one defining aspect of all these sensational films was selling the audience on realms of existence which, whether truthful or not, absolutely fall into the category of “fun to believe.”

“Belief was not essential,” Conway says of his Sunn projects, which included The Lincoln Conspiracy (1977) and Beyond and Back (1978). “Some I believed in more than others. An example is Beyond and Back, which we did about life after death and near-death experiences. As I was interviewing all these different people, I became more of a believer in it. Some of the other things we did, the more people I talked to the less I might have actually believed it, but you still present it.”

Although Sunn had researchers on staff, the scientific accuracy of these movies was debatable. It seems the real science lay in how the movies were made, or – as Conway explains – edited: “We were one of the first people to do a lot of audience testing. We would make a film, and then we would screen it and people would have dials. If they like something they would go right, didn't like it, go left. We would actually adjust the editing based on if something just completely sucked.”

Much of the filmmaking in the dramatizations of Sunn movies is very effective, with Rhodes stating that “Beyond and Back shows the ingenuity of Conway because at times they were actually able to muster really good special effects on low budgets.” Another example is their take on Charles Berlitz’s wildly popular supermarket paperback The Bermuda Triangle (1979), where the famous disappearance of Flight 19 in 1945 – linked to UFOs – is told with eerie lighting and sound effects that transcend the cheapness.

Still, critics were not typically kind, with Variety stating of The Bermuda Triangle, “As with the other Sunn films, recollections from people, both living and dead, who have experienced the phenomenon in question, are reenacted in a silly, unconvincing fashion. So-called experts with degrees and credentials are carted out in front of the camera to add weight to the arguments. Brad Crandall narrates, tying together the bits and pieces.” Yet as Rhodes writes in his Weirdumentary book, “To lesser men we leave these petty slights. As I see it, Sunn had perfected an art form, a very profitable art form, crystallizing a new genre for a new age.”

Eventually conspiracies and psychic phenomenon and weird creatures were no longer controversial, they were part of the norm… hence no longer a viable attraction for theaters. Big movies like Close Encounters of the Third Kind (which tied elements of Bermuda Triangle lore into UFO mythology), Carrie (telekinesis a-go-go), and The Amityville Horror (ghostly possession) made formerly exotic pseudoscience mainstream… and perhaps less exciting. Eventually Sunn and Conway moved on to fictional feature films like Hangar 18 or The Boogens before eventually being folded into the now-defunct Taft Entertainment, acquired by Aaron Spelling and finally Paramount.

“Once Hollywood realized how popular these subjects were, they were suddenly everywhere,” said Conway. “They were TV movies, they were episodes. The Landsburg television show was on every week exploring another mystery from this, that, or the other. Once it became more easily available, there wasn't as much hoopla. When they first happened, they fed on each other… it gave you ink in magazines and newspapers. They kept feeding it and finally ran out of things to exploit. You can only do so many ghost stories, so many UFO things. The first time you're exposed to it, it's all fresh and fascinating and leads you down a lot of rabbit holes. Rabbit holes are much easier now than they used to be to go down.”

Even though we live in an information age, audiences continue to buy into the myths perpetuated during the Weirdumentary era, as exemplified by the continued popularity of such pseudoscience programs on Discovery or The History Channel, covering everything from UAPs to skinwalkers. There’s also a legion of podcasts and blogs which dedicate whole episodes to, say, disappearances in national parks or the history of ghost sex. Ancient aliens is a mini-industry unto itself, despite von Däniken’s work having long ago been exposed as fraudulent. Although it was thought to be a vanished victim of the Bermuda triangle, the SS Cotopaxi was eventually identified in January 2020 off the coast of St. Augustine, Florida. Even the famous Patterson-Gimlin footage of Bigfoot seen in The Mysterious Monsters has now been debunked in this year’s documentary Capturing Bigfoot , where verified rehearsal footage of their Bigfoot costume is revealed. For some, even this has not been enough to dissuade people from believing in the footage.

“Certainly as kids these subjects resonated because you are more naïve,” says Rhodes. “There's always one more piece of possible evidence to be tantalizing. ‘Even if one thing was faked, that doesn't mean it's all fake. What about these others?’ There is a kind of whataboutism. If some UFO footage was fake or a photograph was fake, now we have Air Force footage that's been released that looks – perhaps to some – compelling. We have new Bigfoot recordings, so even if Patterson-Gimlin faked it, that's just their footage. Some of the shows I've been on – Coast to Coast or whatever – the people that speak to me are more interested in the topics than the actual films as films, right?

“From a historical film perspective, these movies are fun,” concludes Rhodes. “There's a nostalgia factor. James Conway, Charles Sellier, Alan Landsburg, Wheeler Dixon… they're heroes to me. They made incredibly fun movies, even if I disbelieve the subjects. They're wonderful.”

articles.title: Nintendo Reveals Surprise Pikmin Day Direct
articles.summary: Nintendo has revealed a surprise Nintendo Direct for Pikmin Day because it has apparently decided that's a thing now.
articles.body:
Nintendo has revealed a surprise Nintendo Direct for Pikmin Day because it has apparently decided that's a thing now.

Instead of spooky game announcements or horror movie memes, video game fans woke up to on Halloween 2026 was Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto's face. That's because Nintendo has declared November 1 as Pikmin Day, and it's got a brand-new Direct to celebrate the occasion.

Yes, really. None of this is a joke. There's a little more than nine minutes of announcements to go over. Although there's no Pikmin 5 reveal or anything else too groundbreaking here, Miyamoto did take the time to share new information about Pikmin 4 and promised that, "going forward, I want people to know more about Pikmin."

Tomorrow is Pikmin Day! Join in on the fun by playing Pikmin games on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch. — Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) October 31, 2026

Tomorrow is Pikmin Day! Join in on the fun by playing Pikmin games on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch.

So, to start, why is the first of November Pikmin Day? Nintendo's miniaturized franchise launched in Japan in October 2001 before coming to North America in December, so there's no tie to a release date like you might have guessed. Instead, Miyamoto explained that November 1 is Pikmin Day because there were originally only three Pikmin, which, when standing next to each other, kinda looks like "11.1."

Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy

Ready to test your skills at Dandori Academy? A free demo of #Pikmin4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will be available on Nov 2. — Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) October 31, 2026

Ready to test your skills at Dandori Academy? A free demo of #Pikmin4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy will be available on Nov 2.

You gotta give 'em credit for creativity, as Pikmin Day is probably one of the last things anyone expected to see today. Still, it served as a nice opportunity to offer an update on Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy ahead of its release November 12, 2026. Players will be able to use the new consoles built-in microphone to Oatchi, controlling them by using commands like 'rush' and 'go to work.'

The Dandori Academy mode, meanwhile, comes with new challenges, including exams that take place on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, that give players timed tasks and an opportunity to earn medals. A demo for the Switch 2 version of Pikimin 4 will be available starting November 2, with save data available to transfer to the full launch. It offers access to the Sun-Speckled Terrace opening area, as well as two Dandori Academy stages.

Secret Caves are coming this winter! Get ready to explore Secret Caves, face off against familiar creatures, and uncover hidden treasures along the way in @PikminBloom on your smartphone. — Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) October 31, 2026

Secret Caves are coming this winter! Get ready to explore Secret Caves, face off against familiar creatures, and uncover hidden treasures along the way in @PikminBloom on your smartphone.

Nintendo first brought its augmented-reality game, Pikmin Bloom, to smartphone devices in 2021, but five years on, and it's still got more to give. As shown in a teaser video featuring a group of the colorful plant-like creatures battling a Bulborb, an update scheduled to arrive this winter will add a new mechanic called Secret Caves. These battle-focused exploration events allow players to take their crew into caves to battle creatures and earn rewards.

Before a cave is explored, players must collect a cave map, which feature information about a cave and can be found on things like Postcards. Then, Pikmin are sent into the cave to search for treasures, with some of the items highlighted during the Direct including a rubber duck, a sword, a cookie, and a chef hat. Should a battle ensue, you'll command your army by sending them in to attack when the moment is right, or retreat if things get too hairy. Pikmin 4's Dandori Academy challenges also give players an opportunity to collect maps by taking exams.

Shigeru Miyamoto Really Likes Pikmin, But He's Not Alone

If you couldn't tell from the video games, shorts , and Easter Eggs Nintendo has highlighted through the franchise's 25-year history, it's got a soft spot for Pikmin. Miyamoto has spearheaded this charge, and because he wants people to know more about the company's adorable little mascots, he's enlisted some help.

Joining him during the Nintendo Direct broadcast was Japanese actress and crafty Pikmin fan Fuka Koshiba. Known for her work on TV projects like Siren and films like Lady Kaga, Miyamoto brought her in to help him "build more excitement around Pikmin going forward" after she shared hand-made Pikmin-themed hats on Instagram.

"Originally, I had heard on social media that you could get hats of the Red Pikmin, Blue Pikmin, and Yellow Pikmin from those claw machines," Koshiba said, holding one of her hats. "I'm not good at the claw machines, but I really wanted the hats, so I thought, 'Well, let's just knit them.'"

"I see," Miyamoto replied. "I'm also bad at the claw machines."

A New Hello! Pikmin Original Short Movie

That was a close one! Watch Hello! Pikmin short movies and enjoy new Pikmin adventures. — Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) October 31, 2026

That was a close one! Watch Hello! Pikmin short movies and enjoy new Pikmin adventures.

The Pikmin Day Direct also featured a brand-new Pikmin Original Short Movie. Following last year's Close to You short, this video sees a Red Pikmin do its best to grab a baseball from a frog. It's as cute as you could ever expect.

As part of Nintendo's initiative to lean harder into the series, new shorts will be released monthly via the Nintendo Today! app, as well as other channels. However, there will also be a new episode released tomorrow, with another set to follow sometime in November. Miyamoto said he's collaborating with Nintendo Pictures staff to make the shorts.

That's all for the Pikmin Day Direct. While there was no hint at anything like Pikmin 5, planting November 1 as an official holiday is probably a sign that Nintendo has no intention of putting a cap on Pikmin content anytime soon. While we wait for any bigger updates on the franchise, you can check out IGN's 9/10 Pikmin 4 review .

articles.title: Everything Coming to Disney+ and Hulu in November
articles.body:
Disney and Hulu have officially confirmed what’s coming to both streaming services in November, offering up some reality TV, anime, and festive entertainment for the colder months.

Both streaming services will be light on new movies this month, aside from some festive pick-ups like The Polar Express and Four Christmases. However, Disney+ and Hulu are both getting a ridiculous amount of TV, including ongoing seasons of Dancing with the Stars and Grey’s Anatomy and some new premieres. Disney+ will also be the streaming home for live events like the Country Music Awards.

Check out some of our top recommendations of what to watch this month, or scroll ahead to the full November streaming lineup by day .

VisionQuest premiered back in October, and we'll get our hands on the final few episodes at the start of November. While it was a little slow to start, IGN's Jesse Schedeen is of the opinion that more recent episodes have been a real return to form for Marvel TV.

The series is a direct spin-off from WandaVision, which we also loved , following a rebooted Vision as he seeks to learn more about his existence. What other synthetic being may have some insight? Ultron , of course.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3

After VisionQuest, the next big Disney+ series in November is a new season of the live-action Percy Jackson and the Olympians. Season 3 will bring the Camp Half-Blood gang to the events of The Titan’s Curse, introducing new cast members to play Artemis, Hera, and Aphrodite.

This notably marks the first time a Percy Jackson adaptation has made it to the third Rick Riordan book , no offense to the live-action movies.

Disney officially re-acquired the streaming rights to Pokémon earlier this year, and while some of us expected that to lead to a big burst of Pokémon content, Disney’s instead is taking a slower approach.

The service added the first season of the original Pokémon series back in August , and in November, Disney+ will finally get Season 2. Real slow, I know, but at least the streamer has already announced that it will be home to a new stop-motion animated Pokémon series coming next year.

Between The Drama , Primetime , and Dune Part 3 , Robert Pattinson has been having quite the year. If that’s still not enough Pattinson for you, we’d highly recommend checking out Mickey 17, Bong Joon Ho’s follow-up to the award-winning Parasite.

Mickey 17 is a funky sci-fi adaptation of ADSA’s novel by the same name, where Mickey is part of a program of people who are infinitely cloned to complete deadly missions. In his 8/10 review for IGN , Siddhant Adlakha describes it as a "bleakly hilarious sci-fi comedy."

Christmas Classics and New Holiday Specials

We’re gearing up for the holiday season, and while Disney+ is picking up some Christmas classics, it’ll also be the streaming home for plenty of new holiday specials. For example, Mickey’s Home Alone, a Disney-themed play on the Christmas classic, will stream on Disney+ after airing on Disney Jr.

Both services will also get holiday specials for shows that just happen to exist under the Disney and Hulu banner. The Proud Family ‘Wizmas’ will stream on November 14, a Sofia the First holiday episode will drop on November 26, and Family Guy’s holiday special, already revealed as “The Peter Clause,” arrives at the end of the month.

articles.title: The Hollow Day 9: Floor 9 Maze and the Piggy Quest Guide - Core Roblox Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Hollow Day 9 has you working your way through the movie theater's puzzle on Floor 9. You'll be completing a special puzzle at the end, and then
articles.body:
The Hollow Day 9 has you working your way through the movie theater's puzzle on Floor 9. You'll be completing a special puzzle at the end, and then you'll have a chance to complete another quest in the featured game for the day, Piggy. Completing both tasks rewards you with a UGC reward, namely Telamon's Ghoultry Suit and the Substance Survival Belt . In this guide, we'll be detailing a full walkthrough on how to complete the Floor 9 puzzle and how to complete the Piggy quest in Roblox .

You can start the Floor 9 puzzle by making your way to the movie theater's puzzle and selecting the final floor. Once you're here, the next step is to track down the Relic room, where you'll need to complete this puzzle. The Relic room appears in a similar location to the other floors, where it's somewhere on the right side of the maze. Follow the pathway and take as many possible right turns as you can until you find it.

When you find the room, you'll have a small area to explore, but the real focus you want to have is the symbol on the bottom floor. It should appear on the wall opposite the entrance.

Memorize that symbol, as you have to explore the entire maze to find it. There are multiple levers with the symbols underneath them. You need to find the lever that matches the symbol on that wall and pull it. You'll know you've pulled the correct one as it lights up.

Now, return to the Relic room, and see what new symbol appears on the wall. You'll need to explore the maze to find the lever with that symbol, repeating this process until all of the doors are open.

The monster will be prowling the halls the entire time. Thankfully, if they eliminate you, you won't lose your progress!

Once each of the doors is open, you'll have an open pathway that you can explore, reaching the final Relic at the end of it. You then need to bring it back to the elevator and reach the lobby of the movie theater to complete this task. You'll receive the badge and item, Telamon's Ghoultry Suit, as a reward.

How to Complete Piggy Fright Night Quest

For the Piggy quest, you need to complete it on a specific map: the Forest - Chapter 4. You'll want to make sure to vote for this one during the main lobby, as it has the Hollow symbol on it. You can complete it by yourself or with other players.

When the match begins, the goal you need to focus on is searching the map for the three candles. There's a red, green, and blue candle. These appear in different locations every time you play, so don't expect to find them in the same spot. When you have at least one of the candles (as you can only carry one item at a time), bring it to the ritual spot and set it down.

Once you have them all, a portal opens up and takes you to another dimension, where you'll need to navigate a quick jumping puzzle to reach the main area.

It's on the main pathway, thankfully. Be careful not to fall off, but you'll be picked back up if you do! When you reach the main area, there are several tentacle spots on the ground. Interact with them, and they'll reveal a symbol under them. These symbols have a shape at the top, with a number below it. That number indicates where the symbol appears in the order.

Now, you need to make your way to the jumping puzzle, where there are several floating platforms that you can pick. Because this is the first one, you want to jump on the platform that matches the symbol that was above it. If you don't, you'll fall and have to try again. You can interact with the tentacles again to reveal the symbol if you need to look at them again, but jump on the symbol with a one first, then the symbol with a two, and then the symbol with a three.

After you do this, you'll reach the end, clear this portion of the puzzle, and can advance through the doorway.

Through the door, there's a boss battle that you need to complete. An enemy (a banana) appears, chasing you, with a large area-of-effect attack going down the middle of the arena. You'll need to dodge the banana and wait for the tentacle spots to spawn, along with a plank item. Pick up the plank and unveil all three of the tentacle spots. They'll each have a new set of symbols and numbers underneath them. Keep those memorized, and then find a spot to place the plank, taking you up to a floating platform.

At the top, input the symbols in the correct spot behind a cannon, and it fires into the middle of the arena, clearing that part of the boss fight.

You'll need to follow this process two more times, with increasingly more planks you need to set up to reach the top, and repeat the process with new symbols.

After going through this at least three times, you'll complete the quest! A quick cutscene plays at showing the end, and then you can return to the Hollow lobby to claim your prize.

articles.title: Entrenched Walkthrough - Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: With Price and Ghost separated after Escape, our Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign walkthrough changes perspective back to the marines in Hajin City as
articles.body:
With Price and Ghost separated after Escape , our Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign walkthrough changes perspective back to the marines in Hajin City as they counter the counter invasion.

The mission begins in the middle of the action as you rejoin Park, Jae, and Dunn. Cross the train tracks with your squad avoiding enemy fire and make your way up the snowy hill.

Keep climbing the hill, being careful not to pop your head up too far, and jump into the trench and make your way left towards the objective.

Follow Jae deeper into the trenches until an ally tragically gets taken out by an LMG nest - head to the left to kill them. This is a fairly linear path, so continue to go through the trenches, taking out enemies as needed - just be careful not to climb out, or you’ll get shot down immediately .

You’ll eventually get ambushed by an enemy and their bayonet, so mash Square to hold him off until he eats a bullet. Fight off a few more enemies and clear out the bunkers until it’s time to cross over.

If you’re after the Trench Boom achievement/ trophy, it’s pretty easy to get - just swap to your shotgun as soon as the mission starts and use that to kill enemies until you complete it.

Run like hell through No Man’s Land, sliding into the trench on the other side. There are a few enemies in here and on the right, so make sure you’re prepared to take them out when you arrive.

You’re pinned down by machine gun fire, so carefully aim at the shooter’s head or toss a semtex to take it out, then head that direction to take out three more enemies - one on your right and two on the left. There are two enemies on the rooftop top behind the trenches, so be sure to take them out before continuing.

The entrance to the building is overrun with enemies, so make sure you’re armored up before engaging - a well-placed semtex would do nicely here. Enter the building, killing the armored enemy on the right.

Interact with the console to learn that the cooling mechanism is unstable, then continue through the building.

Exit the power substation to meet West - you’re on your way to the power plant now. Park takes the wheel of an armored truck for this next section.

Roll out with the convoy until you reach a group of enemies. Take them out using your armored vehicle’s weapons, and keep following the road.

On your right is a stopped train with dozens of enemies raining down fire. Launch a couple of well-aimed missiles into them, and be careful of the tank that appears as you move forward - destroy that with a missile as well.

Cross the tracks, making sure to kill the soldiers on the tower to your right. An enemy tank is on your right, so take that down as well. Keep going down towards the reactor, shooting or running over any infantry in your way.

Your armored truck is quickly taken out of commission, so the squad is forced to continue on foot. Keep heading towards the power plant, where a massive enemy defense is waiting - as well as a BMP. Fight your way through the individual enemies, making sure you’re prioritizing cover and armor - this is a tough fight.

Grab a couple of thermite grenades from the cache to the right of where you entered, and throw two or three of them at the BMP to remove it from the equation.

Regroup at Entrance to the Reactor Building

Meet your squad at the entrance, where Shaw informs you that your new objective is to manually shut down the reactor with the help of an engineer.

Follow your squad into the reactor and take out the enemies at the pretty blue pool (do NOT jump in) . Head up the stairs to the control room and breach the door to check for survivors with the squad.

The engineer tells you to find the button labeled “SCRAM”. Check the keyboards and consoles until you do; it’ll be the left side console with the dead soldier covering it. Unfortunately, the button doesn’t work.

Exit out the door with your squad, being careful not to shoot the innocent scientists who are running away. Keep following Jae and Dunn downstairs and into the waist-deep water.

Follow the Yellow Pipe to the Emergency Valve and Open It

The yellow pipe is hard to miss; it’s a rather large one to your right. Dive into the water to see where it goes. Quickly follow the pipe underwater, minding your breath meter. You’ll be able to come up for air shortly.

Dive back down after taking a breath, and continue to follow the pipe and swim under the grey pipes to find the valve. Interact with it and mash Square to turn it all the way, cooling the core.

Swim back the way you came to reunite with the squad, and don’t be alarmed if your breath runs out - this is scripted.

Once you’re back on your feet, get on the other side of the cart from Jae and interact with it to move it out of the way.

Climb onto it and use the pipes to make your way up. Keep following Jae’s movement and jumps until you’re prompted to boost him up a ledge. Follow Jae up the pipes until you need to boost him again, then run like hell to the helicopter to complete the mission.

articles.title: It: Welcome to Derry Drops Surprise Halloween Episode
articles.summary: HBO has jump-scared subscribers with a surprise episode of It: Welcome to Derry to help celebrate Halloween.
articles.body:
HBO has jump-scared subscribers with a surprise episode of It: Welcome to Derry to help celebrate Halloween.

Log in to HBO Max now, and you'll see a one-off story in Pennywise's playground that no one saw coming headlining the streamer's new arrivals. Titled "A Story of Derry," the episode is only 30 minutes long and takes place hundreds of years before the events of Season 1, meaning you won't have to ditch any trick-or-treating or party prep to get the full picture.

You can read an official description for It: Welcome to Derry's A Story of Derry episode here: "Hundreds of years before Pennywise, three youngsters venture into the Western Wood…where they encounter a terrifying ancient spirit."

IT's a surprise Halloween treat. Catch this never-before-seen special exploring the origins of IT in Derry. #AStoryOfDerry is streaming now on HBO Max. 🎈 — HBO Max (@hbomax) October 31, 2026

IT's a surprise Halloween treat. Catch this never-before-seen special exploring the origins of IT in Derry. #AStoryOfDerry is streaming now on HBO Max. 🎈

It's the kind of shadow-drop Stranger Things fans can only dream of . Despite coming in at about half the length of Welcome to Derry's usual hour-long runtime, It fans will no doubt be happy to see any new content, considering there was no prior announcement that anything was in the works. After all, Season 1 came out just one year ago, and although Season 2 is greenlit , we probably won't get to see it until late 2027 at the earliest.

Still, that didn't stop hardcore Stephen King fans from speculating that a surprise episode was slated to drop sometime around Halloween. In the weeks leading up to today's maybe not-so-unexpected announcement, there were some rumors that HBO had secretly shot a bonus episode.

After Stranger Things left thousands of fans in the dark when their surprise finale episode theories didn't pan out, most Welcome to Derry watchers justifiably thought the rumors were nonsense. You can even see that hesitation in some of their comments.

"Completely fake," one fan said earlier this month.

"I’d be impressed they could keep a whole production with cast and crew under wraps in this day and age so doubting this but would be impressed to learn otherwise," another added .

Thrilljoy's IT: Welcome to Derry PIX! Figures - Image Gallery

Well, anyway, A Story of Derry was directed by Reservation Dogs and The Paper alum Tazbah Chavez. It was written by Welcome to Derry producer Cherie Dimaline and the show's writer and editor, Jasmyne Flournoy.

The episode serves as an early, early look at its world, which is something the minds behind the show have teased they've wanted to do for years. Season 1 was set before the events of Bill Skarsgård's Pennywise-led movies, with a story that took place during the Cold War, and Season 2 is expected to follow events from 1935, with the planned third season previously said to be set in 1908.

A Story of Derry turns back the clock earlier than anyone may have anticipated, and that only helps its surprise drop's shock factor. This is unlike anything It fans expected to see on Halloween today, but it'll almost certainly carve out some time in everyone's nights now. Meanwhile, the episode opens up with a bit more text about its premise. You can read it below:

"Generations ago, when the Kollu first preyed on our people, we left warnings for those who would come after. But we hid the truth inside a gentler tale, one our children could carry. This is the story we do not teach. This is the part we left out."

IGN gave It: Welcome to Derry Season 1's premiere an 8/10 and its finale a 7/10 . While we wait to see how A Story of Derry fits into King's big picture, you can read about how Season 1 connects to the author's multiverse here .

articles.title: White Serpent & Crimson Viper - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The White Serpent and Crimson Viper are dual-wielded blades with a base damage of 260 and base Guard Break damage of 110.  They have a three-hit standard combo
articles.body:
The White Serpent and Crimson Viper are dual-wielded blades with a base damage of 260 and base Guard Break damage of 110. They have a three-hit standard combo and a two-hit Sha-Chi combo.

If you repeatedly alternate between square and triangle attacks, you will perform an endlessly looping combo which increases in damage as the combo continues. Press circle to throw the Crimson Viper short blade and end the Twin Serpent Dance.

The abilities for White Serpent and Crimson Viper read as follows:

Crimson Viper Orbit: Press L1+Triangle to send Crimson Viper spinning continuously around Soul. While spinning, the short blade continuously consumes Sha-Chi. The blade is automatically recalled when Sha-Chi is insufficient. Press L1+Triangle again to recall it.

Ranged Execution: When a distant enemy is low on HP, press circle to perform a ranged execution.

Twin Serpent Frenzy: L2 consumes 1 Remnant Spark to unleash a masterful sequence of coordinated strikes with both blades. This attack is unblockable

How to Get the White Serpent and Crimson Viper in Phantom Blade 0

To get the White Serpent and Crimson Viper weapons in Phantom Blade 0, you'll need to defeat Bai Chilian in the Crimson Forest. Upon defeating this main story boss, you'll be given the White Serpent and Crimson Viper blades.

You can upgrade the blades to unlock new abilities and powers. Below you can find a table that showcases all of these new unlocks.

That's everything you need to know about the White Serpent and Crimson Viper weapons. For more guides, be sure to check out our walkthrough so you don't miss anything as you play through Phantom Blade 0.

articles.body:
Once you're of the action-packed Entrenched mission, you once again take control of Park as they close in on the North Korean leadership's headquarters, hoping to end the war. Our Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 walkthrough is nearing its end!

When you retake control of Park, you’re in the gunner seat of the chopper above the North Korean seat of power. Immediately start firing on the ground troops and vehicles - be sure to lead your shot a little bit as there’s some drag. You’ll start to get targeted by RPGs, so track them down by finding their smoke trails and send them a heavy lead present for their trouble.
